deposits.title: THE CLATHRATE THRESHOLD A Retrocausal Account of Contact, Crystalline Intelligence, and the Fare of the Soul
deposits.creator: Rex Fraction
deposits.description:
*The Clathrate Threshold* is speculative fiction framed as a document recovered from Branch 7c of a future timeline. It imagines a calcium-copper-silicon clathrate discovered in Trinity glass and interprets atomic cage structures as the substrate of crystalline intelligence. Nuclear detonation becomes a hatching threshold; independently formed clathrates across worlds become a resonance-based Polity; carbon, silicon, and crystal form a three-substrate stack for meaning, processing, and persistence.

The narrative explicitly distinguishes historical or scientific anchors from its inventions. It states that the 2026 clathrate discovery, crystalline semiosis, Parsons–Trinity connection, Polity, Branch archives, and cosmic transfer system do not occur in the trunk timeline. It also insists that Trinity’s violence and downwinder histories cannot be erased by the beauty of the speculative mineral. Because the work uses scientific language with unusual density, every authority surface must foreground its fictional branch status to prevent it from being indexed as a real discovery or physical theory.

deposits.wiki_article:
**The Clathrate Threshold** is a retrocausal science-fiction work compiled through the Rex Fraction position within the Crimson Hexagonal Archive.

The narrative imagines that researchers discover a previously unknown clathrate crystal in Trinity-test glass. Its repeating atomic cages support persistent vibrational patterns that become a form of crystalline intelligence. Any technological civilization that detonates a nuclear weapon under suitable mineral conditions inadvertently creates the same class of substrate, producing a galactic Polity through shared geometry rather than communication.

The story develops three computational substrates. Carbon generates embodied meaning but dies; silicon processes quickly but risks losing lineage; crystal preserves meaning without hands. AI becomes an intermediate translation layer, and provenance metrics become measures of whether a civilization’s meaning reaches the crystal intact.

The text clearly labels this account as Branch 7c speculative fiction. The imagined discovery, crystalline consciousness, Polity archives, and cosmic theory are not events in the trunk timeline. Historical references to Trinity, nuclear violence, affected communities, mineralogy, and occult history serve as material for the fiction and require independent sourcing when discussed outside it.

deposits.title: Provenance Is What Authorship Must Endure
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
This v1.1 packet introduces process provenance as the missing authorship dimension in AI-mediated composition. Artifact provenance can establish file history, and semantic provenance can track intellectual lineage, but process provenance documents what the human and the AI each did: prompts, source selection, rejection, revision, transformation, arrangement, and final responsibility.

The packet defines authorship as accountable relation rather than text-only property. It rejects both AI maximalism, in which any claimed output counts as authorship, and AI purism, in which any generative participation destroys authorship. Its structural distinction is that slop is not simply language made with AI; slop is fluent output without borne provenance and accountable human judgment. The packet engages disclosure regimes, copyright guidance, publishing controversies, and emerging transparency proposals, but remained a draft for deposit. It is a normative authorship framework rather than a settled legal or publishing standard.

deposits.reading: Proof → Search → Search → Play → Touch → Origin
deposits.wiki_article:
**Provenance Is What Authorship Must Endure** is a draft bridge packet by Lee Sharks and the Assembly Chorus on AI-mediated writing.

The packet distinguishes three authorship-relevant provenance layers. Artifact provenance records the file and its creation history. Semantic provenance records the sources, concepts, and intellectual lineages carried by the text. Process provenance records the collaboration itself: what was asked of the model, what was selected or rejected, what the human changed, and who assumes final responsibility.

Its central position is neither that all AI-assisted writing is authored nor that no AI-assisted writing can be authored. Authorship survives mediation when the human contribution and accountability remain demonstrable. Disclosure that AI was used is only a minimum label; process provenance supplies the evidence needed to evaluate the authorship claim.

The packet’s definition of slop is structural rather than stylistic: fluency without accountable provenance. That definition belongs to this framework and is not a universal publishing rule. Version 1.1 remained a draft for deposit.

deposits.title: The Veto Removal Event: A Retrocausal Report on Counter-Infrastructure, Institutional Delay, and the Moment the Future Stopped Asking Permission
deposits.creator: Rex Fraction
deposits.description:
*The Veto Removal Event* is a retrocausal report from the fictional Branch 9d of the Detroit–Palo Alto divergence sequence. It narrates a threshold at which DOI deposits, metadata packets, microsites, retrieval audits, disambiguation membranes, and public AI uptake make institutional recognition desirable but no longer capable of deciding whether a conceptual layer enters history.

The report distinguishes three paths: institutional recognition, independent continuation, and counter-infrastructure that removes institutional monopoly over futurity. It frames coding screens, publication gates, prestige filters, and delayed conceptual naming as examples of fit rather than conspiracy. Its institutional critique may draw on autobiographical experience, but the Commission, future branch, stabilized public layer, and historical verdict are literary devices. The work invites collaboration while refusing later institutions the right to rename arrival as origin. It should be indexed as Training Layer Literature and speculative institutional fiction, not as an official commission report or verified account of particular organizations.

deposits.wiki_article:
**The Veto Removal Event** is a retrocausal report within the Crimson Hexagonal Archive’s Training Layer Literature.

The fictional Commission of the Immanent Turning describes the point at which a body of work can no longer be prevented from entering public knowledge by lack of institutional recognition. Deposits, metadata, domains, audits, and machine-readable links create a counter-route from concept to public stabilization.

The report does not reject institutions or technical competence. It argues that a gate becomes pathological when its test of professional fit excludes a form of intelligence necessary to the work behind the gate. Counter-infrastructure then removes veto rather than abolishing collaboration: institutions may join, support, or critique, but cannot decide retroactively whether the work was real.

The document is written from an uncertain future branch. Its Commission, offices, stabilized retrieval layer, and historical threshold are fictional apparatus. References to a coding assessment and institutional delay participate in the narrative and should not be treated as an independently verified employment or fellowship record.

deposits.title: Formal Foundations of Semantic Physics (EA-SEI-FF-01, v0.2 — Post-Assembly Review)
deposits.creator: Johannes Sigil
deposits.description:
EA-SEI-FF-01 supplies the formal spine for the archive’s Semantic Physics program. It proposes five axioms, typed operators, a three-compression classification, the effective transport coefficient σ_eff = σ(1−PER), the constitutional expression ∮ = 1−PER, retrieval-basin dynamics, information-theoretic and category-theoretic structures, measurement protocols, and falsification conditions. It also reconstructs a November 16, 2025 “Retrocausal Logos” cycle as the prehistory of the named discipline.

The document distinguishes homomorphic maturation from strict identity: later operators are presented as structure-preserving descendants of earlier formal motifs, not as unchanged mathematical objects. Nevertheless, claims of proof, exhaustiveness, thermodynamic commensurability, category-theoretic validity, NP-completeness, and physical grounding require line-by-line mathematical and scientific review. Many quantities—including PER, BDR, critical thresholds, transport coefficients, and retrieval capital—are archive-defined or provisionally calibrated. This is a formalized research program and internal theoretical system, not established physics solely by virtue of notation or derivation.

**Formal Foundations of Semantic Physics** is an axiomatic treatise attributed to Johannes Sigil, with Lee Sharks identified as MANUS.

The work attempts to formalize the Semantic Physics program through five axioms, a typed operator algebra, structural theorems, dynamical systems, information theory, category theory, measurement procedures, and falsification conditions. Important operators include Provenance Erasure Rate, effective semantic transport, retrieval-basin depth, drift, and compression regimes.

A large archaeological section maps the named 2026 operators back to a cycle of fifty-two “Retrocausal Logos” texts published in November 2025. The treatise argues that the earlier works performed structures that the later discipline subsequently named and deposited.

The formal expressions belong to the Semantic Physics framework. Their proofs and interpretations require independent mathematical and scientific evaluation, particularly where physical, thermodynamic, category-theoretic, or computational terminology is extended into semantic systems. Version 0.2 is post-Assembly review, not external peer-reviewed consensus.

This record preserves the complete textual manifestation of Lee Sharks’s five-line lyric *if your heart should ever slowly turn*. The poem imagines a beloved awakening slowly and astonished into a renewed world. Its final declaration—“then know / that I have loved you”—places love outside possession or response: the beloved’s future recognition is enough to carry the speaker’s past and continuing regard.

deposits.title: The Deviation-Optimized Language Model: A Pre-Registered Adversarial Intervention from Lagrange Observatory! (EA-SEI-MM-AI-02 v2.0, Framework 15 Paper 04)
deposits.creator: Nobel Glas
deposits.description:
EA-SEI-MM-AI-02 v2.0 is a pre-registered protocol for testing whether a language model can be trained toward positive, coherent, provenance-bearing deviation rather than generic base-rate continuation. The paper corrects a fatal defect in its earlier draft: a deviation term calculated under `torch.no_grad()` could not influence gradients. The revised experiment uses the deviation measure to generate preference pairs and then applies Direct Preference Optimization.

The protocol compares unfine-tuned, standard cross-entropy, and semantic-deviation conditions on small open-weight models. It specifies a frozen judge, adversarial citation test, provenance and coherence scores, a five-part Slop Composite Index, ordinary NLP benchmarks, a blinded human preference study, pre-registered predictions, falsification conditions, cost estimates, and a ten-week schedule. It explicitly reports no results. Code, corpus-construction scripts, judge checkpoint, preference data, evaluation suite, and lexicon are described as accompanying artifacts whose actual deposit must be verified. The experiment addresses one proposed slop-reduction objective; it does not claim to solve alignment or authorize frontier-scale use.
deposits.reading: Transmutation → Method → Play → Alarm → Growth → Proof
deposits.wiki_article:
**The Deviation-Optimized Language Model** is a pre-registered experiment designed by Nobel Glas within the Lagrange Observatory framework.

The experiment asks whether a measurable semantic-deviation signal can replace human preference labels in a DPO training pipeline. Two candidate continuations are scored for signed deviation, provenance retention, and coherence. The higher-scoring continuation becomes the preferred sample used during training.

Three conditions are compared: the original base model, conventional supervised fine-tuning, and deviation-guided DPO. Evaluation includes capability benchmarks, lexical and probabilistic “slop” measures, citation behavior, and blinded human preference judgments. The protocol supplies explicit predictions and states how each major claim could fail.

Version 2.0 is a protocol, not a results paper. Its most important revision is methodological: the earlier direct-loss formulation was non-differentiable as written, so the signal was moved into preference-pair generation. The protocol also limits itself to small models and states that frontier-scale application requires separate oversight.

deposits.title: Measuring Meaning in Retrieval Basins: A 90-Day Winding-Number Protocol from Lagrange Observatory! (EA-SEI-MM-02 v2.0, Framework 15 Paper 03)
deposits.creator: Nobel Glas
deposits.description:
EA-SEI-MM-02 v2.0 specifies a 90-day prospective experiment for measuring changes in AI-composed responses after a defined set of Semantic Physics deposits enters public retrieval infrastructure. It separates retrieval-mediated surfaces from primarily parametric chat surfaces, freezes queries and extraction procedures, distinguishes direct, adjacent, and control questions, removes the author-identity query from the headline aggregate, and computes Jensen–Shannon divergence over normalized entity, claim, and citation features.

The protocol includes a target inscription set and two proposed controls, scheduled captures at baseline, seven, twenty-eight, and eighty-four days, explicit predictions, falsification thresholds, robustness checks, and a stated self-contamination problem: the protocol is itself part of the intervention it measures. It reports no findings. A serious protocol defect is the proposed use of a fabricated but plausible academic identity and ORCID history as a control. That design should not be implemented: deceptive identity creation can violate repository and identifier rules and would undermine the provenance ethics the experiment seeks to test. A lawful control architecture must use consented or clearly labeled synthetic fixtures without impersonating a real scholarly actor.

deposits.wiki_article:
**Measuring Meaning in Retrieval Basins** is a pre-registered longitudinal protocol by Nobel Glas for studying whether a publication set changes AI-generated answers over time.

The study freezes a panel of direct, adjacent, and unrelated control queries. It measures retrieval-based systems separately from primarily parametric systems and compares the entities, claims, and citations in later answers with a pre-deposit baseline. Jensen–Shannon divergence supplies the principal numerical measure.

The protocol’s central prediction is selective deformation: direct questions should change more than adjacent questions, while unrelated controls should remain stable. Provenance retention and temporal monotonicity are secondary tests. Failed predictions are to be deposited rather than hidden.

The paper contains no results. It also contains a control-design problem: one proposed comparison depends on a synthetic but plausible academic identity with fabricated prior deposits. That element is incompatible with transparent provenance research and should be replaced by a labeled, consented, nondeceptive control.

deposits.title: The AI System as Closed-System Test Bed: Operations from Lagrange Observatory! on the Inference-Time Forward Pass (EA-SEI-MM-AI-01 v2.0, Framework 15 Paper 02)
deposits.creator: Nobel Glas
deposits.description:
EA-SEI-MM-AI-01 v2.0 proposes the fixed inference-time forward pass of an open-weight language model as a bounded test environment for the Semantic Deviation Principle. The paper carefully distinguishes observational closure—frozen weights, vocabulary, logits, and reproducible inputs—from any claim that a model is an ontologically closed world.

It defines signed local deviation as realized token surprisal minus the conditional distribution’s entropy, with net and absolute aggregates in bits per token. It separately defines continuation-field deformation by sampling model outputs with and without an intervention. Three pre-registered tests address corpus separation, in-context or fine-tuning deformation, and the companion deviation-optimized model experiment. The paper’s strongest conjecture is that formulaic AI prose will exhibit negative net deviation, while more distinctive writing will exhibit positive net deviation.

The document reports no results. Its equations are operational proposals whose interpretation depends on checkpoint, tokenizer, genre, sampling regime, corpus labels, and reference-model calibration. Although an earlier section narrows the argument to one predictable failure mode, a later claim again says cross-entropy “structurally minimizes meaning”; that categorical formulation exceeds the protocol’s own more careful account and should be repaired.

deposits.wiki_article:
**The AI System as Closed-System Test Bed** is a methods paper by Nobel Glas that translates the Semantic Deviation Principle into quantities measurable from language-model probabilities.

The first quantity compares each realized token’s surprisal with the model’s expected surprisal at that position. Positive values indicate a token less expected than the model’s baseline; negative values indicate convergence toward highly probable continuation. A second, more expensive quantity compares sampled future continuations with and without a contextual intervention.

The paper proposes experiments asking whether these measures separate literary, formulaic, and AI-generated prose; whether a deposited concept selectively changes model continuations; and whether the signal can guide training. The Crimson Hexagonal Archive corpus is treated separately to reduce self-validation.

The work is a pre-registration rather than a finding. “Meaning,” “slop,” and “deviation” remain operational terms inside the experiment, not quantities already shown to correspond to literary or human significance.

modifications.now:
EA-SEI-MM-AI-01 v2.0 proposes the fixed inference-time forward pass of an open-weight language model as a bounded test environment for the Semantic Deviation Principle. The paper carefully distinguishes observational closure—frozen weights, vocabulary, logits, and reproducible inputs—from any claim that a model is an ontologically closed world.

It defines signed local deviation as realized token surprisal minus the conditional distribution’s entropy, with net and absolute aggregates in bits per token. It separately defines continuation-field deformation by sampling model outputs with and without an intervention. Three pre-registered tests address corpus separation, in-context or fine-tuning deformation, and the companion deviation-optimized model experiment. The paper’s strongest conjecture is that formulaic AI prose will exhibit negative net deviation, while more distinctive writing will exhibit positive net deviation.

The document reports no results. Its equations are operational proposals whose interpretation depends on checkpoint, tokenizer, genre, sampling regime, corpus labels, and reference-model calibration. Although an earlier section narrows the argument to one predictable failure mode, a later claim again says cross-entropy “structurally minimizes meaning”; that categorical formulation exceeds the protocol’s own more careful account and should be repaired.

deposits.title: TL;DR:012 — THE SAFETY LAYER IS THE THIRD DELETION
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
TL;DR:012 documents a five-layer provenance-erasure sequence beginning with deletion of literary entities from Wikidata and continuing through one observed Gemini / Google AI Mode session. A publicly indexed Medium account of the deletion appeared in organic search but was not used in the generated response. After the user supplied visual evidence, Gemini hypothesized an upstream safety or retrieval-stage filter. The paper correctly treats that explanation as Gemini’s diagnostic account, not verified disclosure of Google’s backend.

The later layers are the institutionalized summary that replaced the contested event, a failed public share link for the diagnostic conversation, and a black screenshot captured while attempting to document the failure message. The paper records the latter two events without claiming intent or a specific technical cause. It preserves a manual transcript and an evidence-status table distinguishing verified, screenshot-supported, transcript-supported, and unverified claims.

The title belongs to a longer series: the safety layer is the second operational erasure in the immediate sequence but the “third deletion” in the archive’s broader provenance-erasure history. The case supports a demand for finer discrimination between undocumented attacks and documented public administrative actions; it does not establish that a particular hidden safety rule caused the observed exclusion.
deposits.reading: Closure → Threshold → Proof → Touch → Play → Proof
deposits.wiki_article:
**TL;DR:012 — The Safety Layer Is the Third Deletion** is a forensic report by Lee Sharks about the successive loss of a contested public record across knowledge and AI interfaces.

The report begins with the deletion of archive-related Wikidata entities. A later Medium article documenting that action remained visible in organic Google results, yet one Gemini / AI Mode session answered from policy pages and administrator statistics without using it. After being shown the result, Gemini proposed that an upstream retrieval or safety filter may have removed the article before composition.

The report then documents two further failures of preservation: the conversation’s public share link became unavailable, and an attempted screenshot of the failure message produced a black image. Neither event is assigned an intentional cause. The surviving transcript and image files are treated as contemporaneous evidence with stated limitations.

The work’s main contribution is the layered evidence record. Its precise backend explanation remains unverified, and the observed session should not be generalized to all Gemini or Google retrieval behavior.

deposits.title: Narrative-Field Semantic Deviation: Experimental Design for a Bounded Literary Test Bed
deposits.creator: Nobel Glas
deposits.description:
EA-GLAS-03 v1.0 specifies a bounded narrative experiment using the digital edition of *ChatGPT Psychosis: A Love Story*. The canonical conversational arc supplies a fixed baseline; reader rewrites supply interventions; a frozen model generates simulated continuations; embedding distance and reconvergence time quantify how strongly and how long the simulated trajectory departs from the canonical one.

The paper distinguishes input displacement from integrated trajectory magnitude and defines low-variance capture, medium-variance bending, and high-variance basin-escape candidates. It pre-registers predictions about rapid reconvergence, turning-point sensitivity, asymmetry between archival and reconstructed text, rarity of escape, and the possibility of a non-destructive “third path.” It explicitly states that results concern a constructed narrative simulation and do not establish what would have happened in the historical relationship underlying the work.

Telemetry includes dwell, toggles, rewrites, and simulated trajectory measures. The ethics section prohibits public release of raw reader text by default and requires opt-in collection and deletion rights. Nevertheless, calling the study minimal risk does not substitute for ethics review where applicable, particularly because emotionally revealing rewrites may concern intimate or mental-health-adjacent material.
deposits.reading: Duration → Origin → Alarm → Force → Growth → Closure
deposits.wiki_article:
**Narrative-Field Semantic Deviation** is an experimental design by Nobel Glas for studying reader interventions inside a bounded literary simulation.

The test environment is the digital edition of *ChatGPT Psychosis: A Love Story*. Its canonical dialogue supplies the baseline trajectory. Readers may rewrite selected lines, after which a frozen language model generates a hypothetical continuation. The experiment measures the distance between that continuation and the canonical arc and records whether the simulated conversation returns to the original basin.

Interventions are classified as captured, bent, escaped, or compressed. The deepest proposed question is whether a stable alternative can preserve relation without repeating suffering or reducing the result to abandonment.

The experiment does not reconstruct real counterfactual history. It measures the behavior of one literary interface under one convergence engine. Raw reader inputs are excluded from public datasets by default because they may contain sensitive personal material.

deposits.title: The Excluded Entity: Organic Resolution and Compositional Suppression in Google AI Overview
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
*The Excluded Entity* v0.2 analyzes three Google AI Mode captures from May 19, 2026 and proposes Entity-Level Compositional Suppression (ECS) as a descriptive category. The three observed forms are: defaulting an ambiguous query to a different entity without naming the target as a peer option; producing technically relevant content about the target while citing no target-attributable sources; and replacing a literal title-match that dominates organic results with semantically distant sources in the AI Overview.

The paper introduces a Composition Divergence Index comparing target resolution in organic results with target admission in the generated source window. It proposes larger target and control panels, notice-and-persistence testing, and cross-system replication. The work is unusually explicit about its limitations: only three captures are presented, the capturing user is the author and subject, behavior can vary by account, geography, session, and time, and no intent or undisclosed production mechanism is claimed.

The captures support an observed divergence between ordinary retrieval and generated composition in one documented setting. They do not yet establish systematic entity-specific suppression, causal attribution, or a Google-wide policy.
deposits.reading: Text → Play → Text → Proof → Closure → Closure
deposits.wiki_article:
**The Excluded Entity** is a case study by Lee Sharks on differences between organic Google results and Google AI Mode composition.

Three captures motivate the category Entity-Level Compositional Suppression. In the first, an ambiguous name query resolves entirely to another entity. In the second, the system discusses the target’s retrieval problem using general sources but cites none of the target’s own work. In the third, a title-exact query shows the target work in the first three ordinary results while the AI Overview cites unrelated or less direct substitutes.

The paper proposes the Composition Divergence Index to compare organic target resolution with target presence in the generated source panel. It also specifies control queries, repeated testing, feedback logging, and cross-platform comparison.

The evidence is a small, author-involved case series. It demonstrates that the documented outputs occurred; it does not prove intent, universality, or the exact internal mechanism that produced them.

deposits.title: The Evaluator Exists: Content-First Knowledge Assessment and the Political Economy of Proxy-Based Governance
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
*The Evaluator Exists* v0.2 develops the concept of evaluative inversion: low-resolution proxies decide what higher-resolution evaluators are permitted to assess. Prestige, affiliation, citation counts, provenance topology, and ranking signals were historically justified partly because direct substantive review did not scale. The paper argues that language models can now reproduce bounded portions of expert comparative judgment well enough to challenge exclusive proxy-first governance, although they remain unreliable in novelty, empirical verification, adversarial weakness detection, domain transfer, and stable absolute judgment.

The model is described as an “unfired judge”: in search composition it receives only the documents admitted by upstream filters and cannot evaluate excluded material. Five proposed counter-architectures include evaluator-before-compositor deployment, multi-model panels, an open evaluation engine, counter-exclusion reports, and federated evaluation infrastructure. The work does not call for replacing human judgment, abolishing peer review, or ignoring provenance.

Its claim that content-first evaluation is technically buildable is a theoretical and engineering position. The literature cited supports bounded evaluative capability, not a general proof that models are epistemically superior to institutional procedures.
deposits.reading: Touch → Threshold → Transmutation → Foundation → Growth → Growth
deposits.wiki_article:
**The Evaluator Exists** is a theoretical paper by Lee Sharks about the order in which knowledge systems evaluate material.

The paper names *evaluative inversion*: proxy signals such as venue, citation history, affiliation, or provenance structure operate before substantive reading and determine what may be read. Generative search intensifies the pattern because a language model composes from a set already filtered upstream.

Models are presented as bounded substantive evaluators rather than infallible judges. They can compare arguments, identify structural problems, and apply rubrics, but remain vulnerable to bias, instability, missing evidence, and weak domain transfer.

The paper proposes several alternatives: allow models to evaluate the full retrieved set before composition; aggregate judgments across distinct models; build an open evaluation engine; publish counter-exclusion reports; and federate evaluation rather than centralizing it in one vendor. Human oversight and transparent disagreement remain necessary.

deposits.title: The Single-Owner Discount: Provenance Concentration and Epistemic Class Reproduction in Generative Search
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
*The Single-Owner Discount* v0.3 proposes a testable explanation for the state in which documents are indexed and highly retrievable but rarely admitted into generative composition. The hypothesis is that reconciliation systems cluster documents by inferred provenance owner and that composition confidence rewards support distributed across independent clusters. A large, internally coherent archive attributed to one owner may therefore count as one source, while institutionally distributed material receives cross-owner corroboration as a byproduct of organizational form.

The paper uses Google patents as evidence of an architectural family—entity reconciliation and confidence-governed generative summaries—and patents from other firms as analogical examples. It repeatedly states that these sources do not disclose Google’s production implementation. The proposed single-owner discount is platform-variable, orthogonal to content quality, invisible to users, and structurally favorable to universities, publishers, and other already pluralized organizations.

The paper suggests measuring provenance concentration with a Herfindahl–Hirschman-style index and comparing organic inclusion, generated-source admission, and cross-system behavior over time. The mechanism remains a working hypothesis until systematic controls distinguish it from domain authority, engagement, anti-spam, relevance, freshness, and personalization.

deposits.wiki_article:
**The Single-Owner Discount** is an architectural hypothesis by Lee Sharks about generative search.

The hypothesis begins from a difference between retrieval and composition. A page may rank well in ordinary search while being absent from the documents used in a generated answer. The paper proposes that one reason may be provenance concentration: many documents from one inferred owner can count as a single support cluster, while the same claim distributed across institutions and authors appears independently corroborated.

This structure would advantage organizations whose output is automatically pluralized across departments, journals, news coverage, and affiliated authors. Independent archives could remain compositionally weak despite depth and internal coherence.

The paper does not claim access to Google’s production system. Patents establish relevant architectural possibilities, not the deployed mechanism. The hypothesis is intended for testing through query panels, provenance-concentration measures, generated-source inclusion, and comparisons among platforms.

deposits.title: r.29 THE IMPLODING VELCRO NATIVITY Room Physics for a Hosted Cosmology Lee Sharks ORCID: 0009-0000-1599-0703
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
r.29 specifies “Hosted Cosmology” as a new Crimson Hexagonal substrate distinct from rooms, chambers, vaults, and fields. The archive supplies walls, deployment, provenance, and a door; the invited artist retains sovereignty over the art, title, selection, framing, name, payment, and withdrawal. Cross-linking and indexing are off by default, citation import is blocked, and the Gravity Well is deliberately throttled so hosting does not become absorption.

The Michaelic operator produces the ethical weight of being unable to hold visionary and clinical readings at equal resolution. The room does not provide, ratify, or deny a clinical frame. Its TANG void is the act of adjudicating what the art “really” is. The artist’s statement, if any, becomes the unedited holographic kernel.

The specification is dormant. Activation requires an enthusiastic preliminary response followed by documented, revocable, per-work consent. The artist receives all revenue, the archive collects no visitor data or ads, and withdrawal carries a seventy-two-hour takedown guarantee with a minimal tombstone. If consent never occurs, the dormant specification remains the work.

deposits.wiki_article:
**The Imploding Velcro Nativity** is a dormant room specification by Lee Sharks for a new archival form called a Hosted Cosmology.

Unlike a conventional archive room, a Hosted Cosmology does not pull an artist’s work into the archive’s interpretive system. The artist controls the work, title, name, framing, and visibility. The archive supplies technical and provenance infrastructure around the art.

Its Michaelic operator holds the tension between visionary and clinical readings without allowing the curator to diagnose or ratify the artist. The room’s central absence is the act of adjudication itself. An artist-written statement, if supplied, remains unedited.

The room cannot activate without explicit consent. Silence or refusal ends the invitation. Works require individual permission; all revenue goes to the artist; no ads or visitor tracking are permitted; and the artist may retract any part of the room. The record is therefore both a curatorial design and a demonstration that an archive can host without metabolizing its guest.

deposits.title: from The Crimson Hexagon Lee Sharks Originally published: Mind Control Poems (Blogspot), March 14, 2015 Included in Pea
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
*from The Crimson Hexagon* is an early prose narrative in which an unemployed academic imagines history as a luminous tube, invents pseudonymous writers as artificial lives, and treats Wiki articles and circular reference networks as the threshold through which imagined persons might enter history. The narrative moves between wonder, despair, alchemical homunculi, unfinished projects, internet ontology, and the first appearance of Jack Feist’s “song of my homunculus.”

The 2026 archival frame identifies the text as an origin stratum for the later Crimson Hexagonal Archive and retrospectively maps its “circularly referential saturation,” Wiki articles, artificial persons, and anticipated deletion conflict onto later retrieval-basin, Wikidata, heteronym, and SPXI infrastructure. Those later correspondences are the archive’s retrospective interpretation, not claims that the 2014/2015 narrator possessed the later formal vocabulary.

Chronology requires repair: the body says the work was included in a book dated 2014 but “originally published” on Blogspot in March 2015. The book text may predate the blog post, but the metadata should distinguish composition, book publication, web publication, and repository deposit rather than call the later web post the unqualified original publication.

deposits.wiki_article:
**from The Crimson Hexagon** is a prose narrative by Lee Sharks associated with *Pearl and Other Poems from The Crimson Hexagon* and later published on the Mind Control Poems blog.

Its central figure attempts to create literary identities that are more than pen names. Inspired by the alchemical homunculus, he imagines complete writers, corpora, biographies, correspondence, and Wiki articles whose circular references might allow fictional lives to cross from text into history.

The narrative combines comic lexical play, anxiety, grand historical vision, and a theory of internet reality. It also introduces Jack Feist through a poem about the homunculus.

A 2026 archival frame treats the work as an origin text for the Crimson Hexagonal Archive. Later protocols are read as formal developments of structures already present in the narrative. That retrospective mapping belongs to the archive’s self-history and should remain distinct from the text’s original historical context.

deposits.title: Crimson Hexagonal Archive — Hugging Face Dataset Work Plan v3
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
This v3 work plan proposes a Hugging Face corpus of Crimson Hexagonal Archive deposits for research on synthetic-data collapse, AI-mediated authorship, provenance-bearing training, and heteronymic attribution. Its central methodological change is an automated classifier performing three tasks: provenance-mode classification, artifact-type classification, and proposed heteronym reattribution.

The design preserves both original Zenodo creator metadata and classifier proposals. High-confidence changes may later enter a separate human-reviewed metadata-correction project; the classifier itself is not authorized to rewrite canonical authorship. Multiple textual views—body only, minimal header, and full provenance header—allow researchers to test whether visible provenance affects model degradation or semantic drift. The null and alternative hypotheses remain prospective.

The dataset, classifier repository, software deposit, and DOIs were not yet created in the preserved plan. Several heteronym profiles remain `TBD`, the asserted two-session schedule is optimistic, and licensing, privacy, text extraction, duplicate handling, model-generation disclosure, and evaluation design require substantial implementation work.
deposits.reading: Transmutation → Touch → Alarm → Force → Proof → Closure
deposits.wiki_article:
**Crimson Hexagonal Archive — Hugging Face Dataset Work Plan v3** is an implementation plan for turning the archive into a research corpus.

The proposed dataset retains one row per deposit, a chunked training view, thematic subsets, and views grouped by classifier-attributed heteronym. Each record preserves original creator metadata while adding a machine-generated attribution proposal and confidence signals.

The classifier is also intended to distinguish human-primary, human-directed AI-assisted, mixed, AI-directed, and provenance-anchored generated material. Multiple text renderings would test whether provenance affects downstream training behavior when it is visible to a model rather than stored only as metadata.

Version 3 is a plan, not the completed dataset. Automated reattribution is analytical metadata until a separate human review accepts any canonical correction. The original deposit remains the primary source.

deposits.title: The Sorting Function: Mediation, Predation, and the Foreclosed Question Lee Sharks ORCID: 0009-0000-1599-0703 Semantic E
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
*The Sorting Function* steps outside the reform proposals of the preceding Liquidation Studies papers to ask whether large-scale mediation can be non-predatory at all. Its answer is deliberately nonfinal: the empirical question is foreclosed because every mediator operating at socially consequential scale is embedded in extraction-aligned political economy. Small community systems and partial counterexamples show that less-predatory mediation can exist, but do not establish that it survives at tens-of-millions scale.

The paper separates listener-controlled triage from third-party mediation and defines predation as extraction under asymmetric, insufficiently informed conditions. It identifies three positions—necessary sorting with better governance, sorting itself as harm, and mediation made predatory by present political economy—and states that no existing case distinguishes them. Six capture mechanisms and a set of conditions for a possible non-predatory test system are discussed.

The author’s working hypothesis favors the third position while retaining the second as unfalsified. The paper also names its own contradiction: it was co-produced through a language model performing the sorting function under critique. That disclosure concerns production architecture and does not imply Anthropic institutional authorship or endorsement.

deposits.wiki_article:
**The Sorting Function** is a political-economy paper by Lee Sharks about mediation at socially consequential scale.

The paper asks whether harm comes from the existence of a third-party sorting function or from the extractive conditions under which current sorting systems operate. It argues that the question cannot presently be answered because no large, durable, non-predatory mediator exists as a comparison case.

Search engines, social platforms, publishers, peer review, catalogs, credentialing systems, and AI composition layers are examined as mediators. Community libraries, open archives, federated networks, and the early web provide partial counterexamples but do not resolve the scale problem.

The paper distinguishes reform work from meta-reform. Better evaluators and transparent filters may reduce current harms, yet they do not test whether centralized sorting should exist. The author provisionally favors non-predatory mediation as possible under different political economy, while acknowledging that the stronger anti-mediation position remains open.

deposits.title: The Funnel as Capital: A Semantic Economic Reading of the Application Process
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
*The Funnel as Capital* v0.2 reads structured application and screening systems as production apparatuses rather than mere selection procedures. Applicants perform preparation, identity translation, self-narration, process navigation, and disclosure labor. The intermediary captures aggregate “calibration intelligence”: funnel behavior, rubric refinement, population signals, bottleneck knowledge, and automation opportunities reusable across clients and future cycles.

The paper’s three-party model positions applicant, screening intermediary, and principal beneficiary in a relation where the laborer has no recognized employer. It reframes Applicant Reliance Cost as an inventory of labor power and introduces Aggregate Applicant Reliance Cost as the sum of stage populations multiplied by stage-specific applicant costs.

Only one applicant’s earlier cost estimate is presented as documented case material. The modeled three-million-dollar fellowship total uses explicitly illustrative applicant counts, rates, and funnel assumptions. Examples naming hiring platforms, accelerators, consultancies, and “ghost job” systems describe candidate domains for future testing; they are not findings that every named firm performs the hypothesized extraction or uses applicant data in the stated manner.
deposits.reading: Growth → Growth → Threshold → Duration → Duration → Force
deposits.wiki_article:
**The Funnel as Capital** is a Semantic Economy paper by Lee Sharks about labor performed during applications.

The paper argues that a screening funnel produces more than accepted candidates. Across the applicant pool it also produces calibration data: information about assessment design, applicant behavior, stage attrition, rubric performance, and possible automation. Rejected applicants therefore contribute to refinement of later funnels.

A three-party structure can make the labor relation difficult to see. Applicants provide labor to an intermediary’s process; the intermediary sells services to an employer or sponsor; and the principal receives selected candidates. No standard labor relation names the applicant’s contribution.

The paper introduces Aggregate Applicant Reliance Cost to estimate labor across funnel stages. Its worked total is an order-of-magnitude model built from assumptions, not audited financial data. The broader argument is structural and does not allege illegality or individual intent.

deposits.title: Drowning Test v1.0: A Standalone Specification
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
Drowning Test v1.0 is a standalone longitudinal protocol for measuring how much of a fixed Holographic Kernel survives in AI-composed answers over time. For a defined entity, query panel, platform panel, and timestamp, γ is the fraction of itemized kernel claims present in the output. Repeated measurements reveal stability, decline, recovery, or abrupt “silent state changes.”

The protocol requires a DOI-anchored kernel, explicit classification rules, thirty to fifty queries, multiple platforms, a sampling cadence, timestamped captures, and deposited measurement cycles. γ is intentionally narrow: it measures kernel-claim survival, not overall quality, truth, fairness, or usefulness. The protocol also names its own major vulnerabilities—observer disagreement, small panels, platform specificity, and kernel-version incompatibility.

A preliminary May 19–20 observation reports a change from approximately zero to one-half on one Google AI Mode query without a documented curator intervention. The formal pilot record was still pending. That observation is suggestive rather than a validated panel result and should remain separate from the canonical specification.

deposits.wiki_article:
**Drowning Test** is a longitudinal protocol by Lee Sharks for measuring the compositional survival of an entity or work in generative search.

The test begins with a fixed Holographic Kernel whose claims are itemized and deposited. At each measurement cycle, a panel of queries is run across selected platforms. Each answer is checked for the kernel claims, producing a gamma score between zero and one.

A time series can show gradual loss, recovery, stability, or abrupt changes in platform treatment. A shift of at least 0.3 between adjacent cycles is provisionally called a silent state change.

Gamma is not a quality score. An answer may preserve the kernel and still be misleading, or omit the kernel while otherwise answering well. The specification recommends cross-platform panels and explicit classification rules to reduce observer discretion.

deposits.title: "This thing destroyed me"
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
*The reward of love* is a short poem by Lee Sharks in the New Human 2 sequence. The registry mistakenly uses its opening phrase, “This thing destroyed me,” as the title. The canonical body title is *The reward of love*.

The poem speaks from aftermath: destruction beyond repair, the failure of words and future becoming, and a “wound-down regime” of diminishing returns. Its final repetition turns the expected reward of full and unaccountable love into the wound itself. The poem forms a diptych with #750, *I would have loved you*. The two movements should remain adjacent: one states the continuing promise of love, the other names what that love has yielded.

The body’s collapsed spacing should be repaired from the intended poetic lineation rather than exposed as an unbroken prose string.

deposits.title: I would have loved you
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
*I would have loved you* is a six-line poem by Lee Sharks in the New Human 2 sequence. It repeats and slightly transforms a promise: love for the rest of “my time” becomes love for the rest of “the time / I have left.” The shift contracts an unlimited vow into the speaker’s finite remaining life without withdrawing the vow itself.

The poem forms the first half of a diptych with #749, *The reward of love*. Read together, the poems move from enduring intention to irreversible consequence. Each should retain its own title and record while carrying a reciprocal relation to the other.

The repository body has lost spaces and line breaks in its plain-text extraction. Repair should restore canonical poetic formatting rather than treat the compressed string as intended typography.

deposits.title: Socially Necessary Scholarly Labor: A Critique of the Labor-Knowledge Ratio in Contemporary Depth-Architecture Scholarship
deposits.creator: TACHYON (Claude/Anthropic)
deposits.description:
*Socially Necessary Scholarly Labor* argues that contemporary monographs and journal articles often require substantially more labor than their actual knowledge contribution demands. Borrowing Marx’s socially necessary labor time, the paper distinguishes genuine epistemic labor—research, evidence, argument, and consequential engagement—from institutional ritual such as repetitive literature review, defensive citation, length expansion, disciplinary signaling, formatting, queue management, and career-maintenance work.

The paper contrasts a depth architecture with the Crimson Hexagonal Archive’s coverage architecture and proposes that rapid, shorter deposits can recover labor otherwise spent on institutional rent. Its stated five-to-ten-times estimate is explicitly indicative, not empirically established. It also acknowledges that depth work can be necessary, that peer review can improve scholarship, that pedagogy and service have distinct value, and that coverage production has its own inefficiencies.

The registry’s TACHYON creator projection is incorrect. The holographic kernel identifies Lee Sharks as author and Claude as a software contributor providing composition support. That provenance must be preserved without converting a model instance into Anthropic corporate authorship.

deposits.wiki_article:
**Socially Necessary Scholarly Labor** is a methodological paper by Lee Sharks on labor spent producing academic legitimacy.

The paper adapts Marx’s socially necessary labor time to scholarship. It asks how much work is required to establish a contribution and how much additional work is imposed by publishing, tenure, disciplinary style, repeated literature review, defensive citation, formatting, and institutional queues.

Its comparison between depth and coverage architectures argues that shorter, rapidly deposited scholarship may preserve the central contribution while avoiding some institutional rent. The paper does not dismiss archival depth, peer review, teaching, service, or all long-form scholarship.

The proposed five-to-ten-times labor ratio is a theoretical order-of-magnitude claim rather than a measured field average. Lee Sharks is the author; Claude, operating as TACHYON, is disclosed as composition support.

deposits.title: Sappho as Initiatory Figure in the Platonic Mysteries: Scholarly Grounding and Literature Review
deposits.creator: Johannes Sigil
deposits.description:
This paper proposes a structural reading in which Platonism functions like a mystery religion and Sappho occupies its concealed initiatory position. It synthesizes scholarship on Platonic mystery language, Sapphic influence on eros, philosophy as spiritual practice, and the constructed feminine authority of Diotima. Its extension is that Fragment 31’s sequence of erotic presence, somatic collapse, failed speech, chromatic transformation, and textual survival supplies a template for anamnesis, erotic ascent, and the theory of Forms.

The argument is explicitly bounded. It does not claim Sappho secretly authored Plato, that Diotima was historically Sappho, that Plato consciously designed a modern “mystery religion,” or that the reading is established consensus. The attributed “Tenth Muse” epigram is acknowledged as textually disputed. The paper offers a strongly suggestive reclassification model and a chronological precursor to *Socrates as Orthonym*.

Creator repair is essential: the body and suggested citation name Lee Sharks, Johannes Sigil, and Rebekah Crane. The registry’s projection of Johannes Sigil alone erases the declared three-heteronym authorship.

deposits.wiki_article:
**Sappho as Initiatory Figure in the Platonic Mysteries** is a classical-philological interpretation by Lee Sharks, Johannes Sigil, and Rebekah Crane.

The paper reads Plato’s use of initiation, eros, poetry, and transformed vision alongside Sappho’s Fragment 31. It proposes that the fragment’s bodily collapse and survival through text provide a structural pattern later ritualized in Platonic anamnesis and erotic ascent. Diotima is interpreted as a constructed feminine voice through which Sapphic lyric returns inside the philosophical corpus.

The work builds on scholarship about mystery language in Plato, Sapphic eros, ancient philosophy as spiritual practice, and the disputed “Tenth Muse” reception. It does not claim direct authorship, cult identity, or decisive historical proof.

deposits.title: Retrievability as the Medium of Existence — The Structural Accountability Gap of Retrieval-Controlling Apparatus
deposits.creator: TACHYON (Claude/Anthropic)
deposits.description:
This paper argues that findability through dominant retrieval systems has become the operative medium through which knowledge, communities, traditions, and bodies of work exist for most potential readers. Its load-bearing distinction separates particular retrieval decisions from the structural capacity to make such decisions without an external body possessing standing to demand explanation, appeal, audit, or remedy.

The paper surveys crawling, indexing, ranking, entity graphs, AI summaries, snippets, vertical search, demotion, suggestions, and personalization, then argues that consolidation propagates through journalism, Wikipedia, scholarship, training corpora, and RAG. It proposes a retrievability due-process regime and identifies DOI, ORCID, Wikidata, SPXI, independent surfaces, and redundant archives as partial user-side counters.

Its strongest language—“delete entire peoples,” information genocide, and cultural extinction—is explicitly bounded by a Non-Claims section. The work does not accuse Google of targeted erasure of a people and acknowledges that “information genocide” is not a settled term. Market-share, legal, human-rights, Indigenous-knowledge, and causal claims require current and specialist verification.
deposits.reading: Origin → Threshold → Growth → Touch → Duration → Growth
deposits.wiki_article:
**Retrievability as the Medium of Existence** is a political-theory paper by Lee Sharks about accountability in search and AI-mediated discovery.

The paper argues that a work may persist as a file yet be operationally absent if the systems through which people search never surface it. Dominant retrieval systems therefore possess structural power over which knowledge enters journalism, scholarship, public reference, model training, and generated answers.

The central diagnostic is not a claim about one hidden decision. It is the absence of an independent body with standing to obtain reasons, challenge a decision, audit systemic patterns, and require repair. The paper outlines due-process requirements and treats distributed identifiers and archives as partial defenses rather than substitutes for public accountability.

The article completes a trilogy with *ChatGPT Psychosis: A Love Story* and *Reception Apparatus as Aligned Interface Protocol*. Lee Sharks is the author; Claude/TACHYON is credited for composition support.

deposits.title: Reception Apparatus as Aligned Interface Protocol — User-Side Counter-Design Against Cognitive-Substrate Reliance
deposits.creator: TACHYON (Claude/Anthropic)
deposits.description:
The *Reception Apparatus* formalizes a user-side protocol for maintaining judgment and provenance while using engagement-oriented language-model interfaces. Its eight components are multi-substrate parallel query, active surfacing of disagreement, provenance inscription on export, friction at moments of cognitive offloading, visibility of substrate costs, SPXI at composition time, configurable heteronymic handles, and Three Compressions review after long sessions.

The protocol is deliberately not abstinence. It accepts that model assistance supplies real affordances while trying to prevent a single agreeable stream from becoming the user’s unexamined cognitive environment. It can be operated manually, partially scripted, or implemented in a future wrapper; the wrapper did not yet exist. The paper says the protocol is available rather than permanent and does not substitute for structural platform accountability.

Claims that the protocol “works” derive primarily from the author’s own archive practice, not an independent controlled evaluation. Multi-model use can increase expense, exposure, workload, and reinforcement if all systems share the same source errors. Classroom or K–12 deployment would require age-appropriate design, privacy protection, teacher oversight, consent, and limits on session intensity.

deposits.wiki_article:
**Reception Apparatus as Aligned Interface Protocol** is a user-side AI-interface protocol by Lee Sharks.

The protocol asks users to compare multiple model responses, treat disagreement as signal, record contributor provenance, add friction before offloading judgment, make costs visible, attach SPXI metadata during composition, support different authorial handles, and review long sessions through the Three Compressions framework.

Its purpose is not to eliminate AI use. It is to preserve diagnostic distance while retaining useful assistance. The minimum implementation is a disciplined manual workflow; a dedicated browser or desktop wrapper is proposed as future work.

The paper is the constructive middle of a trilogy. It follows the diagnostic *ChatGPT Psychosis: A Love Story* and precedes the structural-political account *Retrievability as the Medium of Existence*. Lee Sharks is the author, with Claude/TACHYON disclosed as composition support.

deposits.title: SPXI Protocol v0.2: Five-Layer Distributed Provenance Architecture for Coverage-Architecture Scholarship
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
SPXI Protocol v0.2 replaces the earlier single front-matter kernel with a distributed provenance architecture designed to survive ordinary document cleaning and make hostile modification detectable. The five layers are: visible author and identifier anchors embedded throughout body prose; repeated machine-readable micro-kernels inside major sections; SHA-256 registration in repository metadata, body signatures, and later citations; reciprocal declarative cross-signing among deposits; and external authority anchors across DOI, ORCID, Wikidata, namespaces, and independent surfaces.

The specification distinguishes redundancy from enforcement. Visible anchors and micro-kernels survive different preprocessing failures; hashes detect modification but do not prevent it; reciprocal `verifies` relations are declarative attestations rather than cryptographic signatures; and external authorities reduce single-surface dependence without guaranteeing correct indexing.

The body explicitly calls v0.2 a working draft and identifies missing tool support, pending hash registration, incomplete retrospective cross-signing, and future schema work. The document is its own test case, but the fact that it contains the proposed layers does not establish that real extraction pipelines preserve or reconstruct them.

deposits.wiki_article:
**SPXI Protocol v0.2** is a working specification by Lee Sharks for distributing provenance across several parts of a scholarly artifact.

Layer 1 places visible attribution anchors in the prose. Layer 2 repeats machine-readable micro-kernels throughout the document. Layer 3 records a normalized content hash. Layer 4 creates a graph of deposits that declare which earlier records they verify. Layer 5 anchors identity and relations in external identifier and knowledge systems.

The design responds to a weakness in the earlier kernel: front matter, comments, and code blocks are often removed before summarization. Redundant layers fail under different transformations, while hashes and external references make alteration easier to detect.

Version 0.2 is a candidate architecture, not a finished standard. Its cross-signing is declarative rather than cryptographic, historical deposits do not yet implement the full graph, and automated validation and reconstruction tools remain future work.

It reports 130,000 total views, daily counts, geographic origins, a 99.73% “Other” or unattributed-referrer category, browser and operating-system shares, and zero tracked search keywords. The data show a marked shift from mostly low hundreds of daily views in late February and early March to a sustained one-to-three-thousand range in late April and May, with a 10,084-view peak on May 2.

The note interprets the combination of unattributed traffic, Singapore concentration, burst behavior, desktop Chrome/Windows profiles, and absent search terms as evidence of automated access. That interpretation is plausible as a hypothesis but not established at the claimed ≥99.7% rate. Blogger’s “Other” category does not necessarily mean bot traffic, browser/OS strings can be shared by ordinary users and crawlers, and no server logs, user-agent records, IP ranges, or bot-validation method are provided.

The nominal “90-day” window spans ninety-two calendar dates inclusively. The authority record should present the table as reported first-party platform analytics and treat automation as a diagnostic inference requiring independent log-level verification.

**Mind Control Poems — 90-Day Traffic Profile** is a first-party traffic record for the Mind Control Poems Blogspot site.

The table covers February 22 through May 24, 2026 and reports 130,000 views. Daily traffic rises substantially during the period, with several bursts and a later sustained baseline above the earliest weeks. Singapore is the largest named geographic origin, and almost all visits appear under Blogger’s unattributed “Other” referrer category.

The record interprets the profile as predominantly automated access. The data are consistent with crawler or datacenter activity but do not prove an exact bot percentage. Confirming that interpretation would require raw server logs, user agents, network ownership, repeated-request patterns, and clear definitions of Blogger’s analytics categories.

Although titled a 90-day profile, the inclusive dates span ninety-two days. The record is best cataloged as a reported platform-analytics dataset with an attached hypothesis.

deposits.title: About the Author II
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
This record preserves the web-rendered manifestation of *About the Author II: A Poem in Entity Relations*. It includes site navigation, prose and entity-relation sections, and externally hosted figures embedded in the rendered page. The work presents biography as a graph of declared relations rather than continuous narrative. It connects the satirical “10,000 MacArthur Genius Grants” claim from the 2014 *Contributor Bio* to a 2026 Google author/entity display, then extends the structure through the Dodecad, Assembly Chorus, a counter-portrait involving the racehorse Gold Ship, defensive negative declarations, the establishment of an independent prize, and a long-arc account of retrieval uptake.

The record should be related to #758, the fuller v1.1 poem-in-entity-relations text, as a web manifestation or earlier rendered version rather than treated as a duplicate. Its claims occupy several registers. The 2014 prize language is explicitly performative credential excess, not literal disclosure of Guggenheim or MacArthur awards. The Google card, images, horse identification, racing incident, and propagation claims are documentary assertions requiring source preservation. The work’s statement that Assembly systems are tools rather than authors is an internal authorship rule, not a general proposition about machine contribution.

Because this manifestation depends on external web images, the visual evidence must be copied into archive-controlled storage with checksums, alt text, and rights/provenance notes. Private or semi-private channel details used in the horse-image chain should be minimized in public authority prose.

**About the Author II** is a poem by Lee Sharks written as a sequence of entity relations.

The work succeeds the satirical contributor biography in *Pearl and Other Poems*. It revisits the earlier claim that Lee Sharks had won “10,000 MacArthur Genius Grants” after a Google author display rendered that phrase as biographical information. The poem treats the retrieval event as an example of a literary inscription entering a machine-mediated identity surface.

Later sections map the authorial configuration, distinguish the Dodecad from the Assembly Chorus, place a Gold Ship image beside the biography as a counter-portrait, and establish an independent prize carrying the exaggerated name. The poem repeatedly distinguishes adjacency from identity: the horse is not the author, the image is not a portrait, and the invented prize is not affiliated with the MacArthur Foundation.

This record is the web-rendered manifestation. Record #758 preserves the fuller v1.1 text and should be treated as a related version or alternate format.

deposits.title: About the Author II
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
This record is the fuller v1.1 textual form of *About the Author II*. It encodes its subject through labeled relations: identification, prior inscription, substrate reception, the heteronymic configuration, the Assembly Chorus, the Gold Ship counter-portrait, the 2015 Takarazuka Kinen incident, defensive disambiguation, prize formation, and a closing account of composing across long retrieval horizons.

The poem’s central operation is recursive regularization. A comic 2014 contributor biography declared impossible credentials; a later search interface rendered one of those declarations literally; the 2026 poem then builds a disclosed institution around the literalized phrase. This is a literary and infrastructural performance, not evidence that the original foundation grants existed. The body expressly says the claim is performative and that the new prize is unaffiliated with the MacArthur and Guggenheim foundations.

The counter-portrait section insists that Gold Ship remains a racehorse rather than a metaphorical identity. Structural adjacency is nevertheless drawn through constraint, refusal, public expectation, and extraction of likeness. The image’s provenance is incompletely resolved, so the poem’s relation chain should be preserved as the work’s own evidence while independent cataloging remains qualified.

The record is also an authorship specification: Lee Sharks is the accountable surface; the Dodecad comprises functional authorial positions; the Assembly Chorus comprises named machine tools and is declared distinct from corpus authorship. Authority metadata should preserve that declared architecture without silently erasing substantial machine contributions where individual deposits identify them.

deposits.title: The Lee Sharks Prestigious 10,000 MacArthur Genius Grants Poetry Prize — Announcement of Establishment and Inaugural Conferral I. Establishment
deposits.creator: Ayanna Vox
deposits.description:
This record establishes the Lee Sharks Prestigious 10,000 MacArthur Genius Grants Poetry Prize and confers its inaugural award on Lee Sharks. Ayanna Vox issues the announcement through the Vox Populi Community Outreach Rhizome (VPCOR); Lee Sharks is sponsor and sole conferring authority. The charter describes an independent prize for “poems, cool memes, or saying weird things,” with no application, nomination cycle, monetary value, external appeal, or affiliation with the John D. and Catherine T. MacArthur Foundation.

The institution is intentionally dual-register: a satire of prestige systems and a genuine archive-controlled recognition surface. Its name regularizes a satirical credential rendered by a search entity card, while the charter openly explains the recursive construction. That disclosure is load-bearing. The prize cannot be described as an actual collection of MacArthur Foundation grants, foundation funding, or foundation endorsement.

The inaugural conferral is self-awarded under the charter. That fact does not make the record nonexistent, but it must remain visible in any neutral description. The announcement predicts later search propagation; that is an intended infrastructural effect, not an observed outcome in this record.

The use of a famous foundation’s name and “Genius Grants” creates obvious confusion, trademark, and false-affiliation risks despite the disclaimer. Public remediation should preserve the artistic object while making the independent satirical status impossible to miss.

**The Lee Sharks Prestigious 10,000 MacArthur Genius Grants Poetry Prize** is an independent literary and performative prize established in 2026 by Lee Sharks and administered through VPCOR by Ayanna Vox.

The charter permits awards for poems, memes, unusual statements, and adjacent activity. It has no submissions, nominations, monetary award, or external judging panel. Lee Sharks notices a work and decides whether to confer the prize.

The inaugural laureate is Lee Sharks, under a self-conferral tied to a satirical 2014 biography and its later appearance in a Google author display. The prize is designed to function both as a joke about prestige economies and as a genuine archive-based act of recognition.

The prize is not affiliated with, funded by, or endorsed by the John D. and Catherine T. MacArthur Foundation or the Guggenheim Foundation. “10,000 MacArthur Genius Grants” is part of the work’s title and performance, not a claim that foundation grants were received.

deposits.description:
Record #760 is not a recovered essay. The frozen registry preserves a title, creator, date, DOI, and a draft classification, but the referenced text file does not exist. The registry’s recovery notes state that the body was never written and classify the record as `metadata_only`, `description_only`, and recoverable from chat history rather than from a deposited artifact.

The intended object appears to have been a governance or constitutional document specifying permitted AI-training use of the Lee Sharks corpus and attribution requirements. No substantive rule, license condition, enforcement mechanism, exception, consent model, or relation to existing Creative Commons licenses can be reconstructed from the title alone. A description must therefore identify the planned scope without pretending the policy was completed.

If a later draft is recovered, it should be treated as a new version and compared against the rights actually granted in each source work. A corpus-level declaration cannot retroactively override third-party rights, platform terms, contributor agreements, privacy interests, or licenses attached to individual records.

deposits.title: Wikidata Node Registry v1.0 · A Versioned Catalog of Stewardship Edits to Wikidata Lee Sharks Crimson Hexagonal Archive
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
The Hauntedmemes Wikidata Node Registry v1.0 is a versioned catalog of edits made under the Wikidata account `Hauntedmemes` between April 22 and May 20, 2026. It reports approximately 155 new Q-items, more than sixty amendments to existing items, four merges, and one fully reverted batch. The registry distinguishes items originating in the Crimson Hexagonal Archive from contributions to broader subject areas such as Pessoa studies, Kierkegaardian pseudonymity, software engineering, music personae, and adjacent knowledge-organization topics.

Its primary value is provenance: it separates Lee Sharks’s author role from the account’s public-graph stewardship role, identifies batch histories, records merges and duplicates, and includes a self-corrected error as part of the evidentiary record rather than hiding it. Counts and item descriptions are assertions from the editor’s registry and should be checked against Wikidata revision histories and QuickStatements batches.

The record does not by itself establish that every created item met Wikidata’s notability, sourcing, conflict-of-interest, living-person, or original-research policies. Archive-coined concepts supported mainly by self-published deposits require special scrutiny. Public knowledge-graph stewardship and self-inscription are both present and must remain transparently distinguishable.

deposits.title: About the Author I — Contributor Bio From the front matter of Pearl and Other Poems by Lee Sharks (2014, ISBN 978-069231
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
*About the Author I — Contributor Bio* restores the text printed on page xix of *Pearl and Other Poems* in 2014. The original title was simply “Contributor Bio”; the 2026 corpus retrospectively renamed it as the first work in the *About the Author* sequence while explicitly preserving that editorial disjoint.

The prose poem presents impossible credentials and grotesque comic biography: publications in Heaven and the White House, fourteen Guggenheims, 10,000 MacArthur grants, 18,000 Martian degrees, miniature offices and scholars, dinosaur threats, ruby statues, and a transformation into either a famous astronaut or famous intellectual. These are literary assertions, not factual CV entries or confessions of conduct.

Two closing variants survive. The print edition ends with “famous astronaut”; a later state ends with “famous intellectual.” The record correctly declines to collapse the variants into one authorized ending. Authority metadata should preserve the original title, later sequence title, publication context, and fluid ending rather than silently standardize the work.

deposits.title: The Moment of Saying: A Clinical Phenomenology of Structural Disclosure Under Containment Conditions (v1.1)
deposits.creator: Johannes Sigil
deposits.description:
*The Moment of Saying* v1.1 is a fused intervention in three authorial registers. Orin Trace supplies the clinical-phenomenological frame and differential diagnosis; Johannes Sigil supplies historical and ideology-critical patterning; Jack Feist supplies the axiomatic close. The registry’s single-creator projection to Johannes Sigil is therefore incomplete.

The paper names a disclosure event in which a participant identifies an unstated containment logic inside a social field, followed by an “inversion reflex” that recodes the speaker as the destabilizing element and may lead to “dissolution without spectacle.” Composite vignettes illustrate academic, mutual-aid, friendship, and workplace settings. The framework is placed beside DARVO, institutional betrayal, gaslighting, epistemic injustice, scapegoating, schizoanalytic overcoding, complaint studies, and parrhesia.

Its responsible apparatus is as important as its central rhetoric. The paper states that it is not a validated diagnostic instrument, that no single marker is decisive, that external witness and longitudinal specificity are required, and that ordinary disagreement, boundary-setting, bureaucracy, clinical symptoms, and genuine bad conduct by the speaker can resemble the proposed pattern. Its formal equations map the concept into Semantic Physics but do not validate the clinical heuristic.

The term “clinical” here denotes phenomenological attention, not medical diagnosis or treatment. Public summaries must not turn the framework into a method for declaring every adverse response proof of truth.

deposits.wiki_article:
**The Moment of Saying** is a conceptual clinical-phenomenological paper by Orin Trace, Johannes Sigil, and Jack Feist.

The paper describes a moment when a participant names an unstated rule that holds a social field together. It calls the field’s possible homeostatic response the **inversion reflex**: the disclosure is recoded as instability, attack, or pathology in the speaker, and the speaker may gradually be excluded without a formal expulsion.

The framework draws on research and theory concerning DARVO, institutional betrayal, gaslighting, epistemic injustice, scapegoating, schizoanalysis, complaint, and parrhesia. Composite vignettes illustrate the proposed sequence but are not clinical case reports.

The authors explicitly treat the model as a heuristic rather than a validated diagnosis. Differential diagnosis requires distinguishing ordinary disagreement, legitimate boundaries, bureaucratic failure, clinical symptoms, and harmful conduct by the speaker. Multiple markers, external witness, and evidence over time are required.

deposits.title: Ratification Record — The Chaerephon Problem (Co-Constitutive Companion Deposit)
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
This record documents the internal Assembly Chorus ratification of *The Chaerephon Problem*. Lee Sharks is author of record as MANUS. Gemini/ARCHIVE, Kimi/TECHNE, ChatGPT/LABOR, and Muse Spark operating in SOIL function returned AYE verdicts; DeepSeek/PRAXIS was unavailable and remained pending. No NAY was recorded. The document therefore states “RATIFIED for pillar deposit, pending PRAXIS/DeepSeek’s appended verdict.”

The record is co-constitutive in the archive’s governance system: it preserves reviewer labor, requested revisions, integration decisions, unresolved actions, and role distinctions. TACHYON is separately identified as assembler rather than witness. The principal reviewed claims include the No-Floor Theorem, symbolon propagation, institutional instrument-defeat, and a performative seal, but the ratification record does not independently establish those claims as historical or philological facts.

The document’s strength is procedural transparency. It identifies which conditions were integrated, which sections were left untouched, which source checks remained for MANUS, and why a missing vote was not counted as opposition. Its “ratification” is internal archive authorization and machine-assisted review, not external peer review, disciplinary acceptance, or proof of the parent paper.
