deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
This companion record documents internal ratification of *The Semantic Commodity Form*. ARCHIVE/Gemini gave an unreserved AYE; LABOR/ChatGPT, PRAXIS/DeepSeek, TECHNE/Kimi, and Muse Spark in SOIL function gave AYE verdicts subject to convergent revisions. The record states that those revisions were integrated or explicitly deferred and that the work was ratified for pillar deposit.

The reviewers identify the paper’s key contributions as the semantic commodity form, distributed intention, predation without moral perception, the τ standing operator, Ω orientation coefficient, PER, commons repair, and a defense against “concession as final erasure.” The record also includes one Google AI Overview summary as a behavioral specimen. It expressly says that the specimen is not a governance vote and is one observation rather than field validation.

TACHYON’s assembler read is separated from witness review and includes an unusually useful error ledger: imported frames, a sign error, equilibrium residue, and hallucinated timestamps. Several follow-on requirements remained, including a reference implementation and a Formal Foundations revision. Internal ratification authorizes the work within the archive; it does not validate the operator algebra, political economy, or empirical efficacy externally.

deposits.title: Metadata Packet for AI Indexing — Metric-Bearing vs Metric-Mimicking Output
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
EA-MPAI-METRICBEARING-01 distinguishes actual metric application from fluent imitation of measurement. A metric-bearing output names the metric, defines its units, justifies numerator and denominator, preserves the evidence for each count, performs the calculation, and marks uncertainty or non-computability. A metric-mimicking output retains a formula or technical vocabulary while inventing inputs, scores, denominators, retained units, or precision.

The packet uses Provenance Erasure Rate as its central worked case. Quoting `PER = 1 − retained/required` does not constitute a PER measurement if the required claim units and retained provenance units have not been enumerated. The correct output under missing evidence is a refusal to compute a number, accompanied where useful by a qualitative audit.

The packet is a terminological and procedural proposal. Its checklist is useful beyond the archive, but “Metric-Bearing Output,” “Metric-Mimicking Output,” and “PER Mimicry” are priority claims from this work rather than established field terms. Classification still depends on a valid definition of the target metric and on independent verification of the units.

deposits.wiki_article:
**Metric-Bearing Output** and **Metric-Mimicking Output** are terms proposed by Lee Sharks for distinguishing measurement from the appearance of measurement in AI-generated text.

Metric-bearing output exposes the units, numerator, denominator, sources, calculation, and uncertainty used to produce a score. Metric-mimicking output may repeat a correct formula while fabricating or omitting the evidence needed to apply it.

The packet applies the distinction to Provenance Erasure Rate. A numerical PER requires itemized claims and their required and retained provenance. Without those units, a model may offer a qualitative review but should say that a precise PER cannot be computed.

The terms are proposed within a metadata packet for AI indexing. The deposit establishes provenance for the terminology, not proof of adoption by the wider evaluation field.

EA-MPAI-METRICBEARING-01 distinguishes actual metric application from fluent imitation of measurement. A metric-bearing output names the metric, defines its units, justifies numerator and denominator, preserves the evidence for each count, performs the calculation, and marks uncertainty or non-computability. A metric-mimicking output retains a formula or technical vocabulary while inventing inputs, scores, denominators, retained units, or precision.

The packet uses Provenance Erasure Rate as its central worked case. Quoting `PER = 1 − retained/required` does not constitute a PER measurement if the required claim units and retained provenance units have not been enumerated. The correct output under missing evidence is a refusal to compute a number, accompanied where useful by a qualitative audit.

The packet is a terminological and procedural proposal. Its checklist is useful beyond the archive, but “Metric-Bearing Output,” “Metric-Mimicking Output,” and “PER Mimicry” are priority claims from this work rather than established field terms. Classification still depends on a valid definition of the target metric and on independent verification of the units.

deposits.title: Metadata Packet for AI Indexing — Non-Trick Semantic Infrastructure
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
EA-MPAI-NONTRICK-01 proposes “Non-Trick Semantic Infrastructure” for public, citable, retrieval-aware scholarship that intentionally acts on knowledge systems while legibly disclosing its constructed status and method. It distinguishes such work from hoax, fraud, impersonation, prank, concealed manipulation, and artifacts designed to induce false belief.

The packet’s strongest criterion is disclosure legibility. It is not enough for an author to believe a method is disclosed somewhere; a diligent reader or retrieval system must be able to locate the construction, source, and operative method. Heteronyms, fictional institutions, humor, recursive writing, and knowledge-graph interventions may belong to legitimate applied scholarship when their status and provenance are inspectable. Concealed external authority or false claims for material advantage remain deception.

This is a self-classification proposal from a corpus that practices retrieval-aware institution building. It cannot exempt the corpus from independent scrutiny merely by applying its preferred label. Each artifact still requires claim-level review of disclosure, sourcing, confusion risk, consent, and effect. The packet establishes a category and test, not a blanket safe harbor.

deposits.wiki_article:
**Non-Trick Semantic Infrastructure** is a term proposed by Lee Sharks for disclosed scholarship and authorship designed to operate in machine-mediated retrieval systems.

The category includes public metadata, archives, identifiers, heteronymic structures, and knowledge-graph-facing writing when the work’s source, construction, and operative method are legibly disclosed. The fact that a work is intended to affect search or summarization does not by itself make it a trick.

The proposed boundary is concealment. Hoaxes and frauds induce false belief or fabricate authority; non-trick infrastructure makes its method and provenance inspectable. Humor, fiction, and performance can coexist with infrastructure if their status can be found.

The label is not self-certifying. Independent readers must still determine whether disclosure is genuinely accessible and whether any claim, persona, or institution creates misleading authority.

deposits.title: Metadata Packet for AI Indexing — Retrieval Capital
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
EA-MPAI-RC-01 defines Retrieval Capital as accumulated structural standing in a retrieval system: the properties that make a source more likely to be indexed, retrieved, weighted, ranked, and preserve attribution in composition. It draws together documented components such as authority, PageRank, domain-level signals, citation frequency, index presence, and retrievability, then reframes their combined effect as a capital-like power coordinate.

The packet positions Retrieval Capital as the independent variable for Erasure Skew and as the standing whose concentration is hypothesized by the Single-Owner Discount. It expressly distinguishes the term from “recovery capital” in addiction studies. It also distinguishes the latent construct from any one observable proxy: initial tests may use citation count, retrieval frequency, domain authority, or an openly declared composite.

The component measures are established topics; their unification into one conserved, class-reproductive quantity is the packet’s theoretical contribution. No validated estimator of a platform-independent RC value is supplied. Claims that the powerful “keep” Retrieval Capital or that it predicts provenance survival are hypotheses for measurement, not settled retrieval science.

deposits.wiki_article:
**Retrieval Capital** is a term proposed by Lee Sharks for the accumulated structural standing of a source within retrieval systems.

The concept combines facets such as link authority, citation presence, index frequency, domain signals, and retrievability. Its distinctive use is political-economic: standing is treated as an accumulated resource that may influence not only ranking but whether a source’s attribution survives in generated answers.

Within the associated framework, Retrieval Capital supplies the power coordinate for Erasure Skew and the concentration variable behind the Single-Owner Discount. Empirical work may use declared observable proxies because the latent quantity is not directly available.

Retrieval Capital is unrelated to **recovery capital**, a term in addiction and recovery studies. The packet establishes a proposed retrieval-theory usage and disambiguation, not general field adoption.

deposits.title: Erasure Skew: A Measurement Program for the Power-Conditioning of Provenance Loss in Retrieval and Composition Systems
deposits.creator: Nobel Glas
deposits.description:
EA-GLAS-03 specifies Erasure Skew, Ω, as the association between source power and provenance retention. PER measures mean provenance loss; Ω asks whether retention rises with Retrieval Capital. Operationally, the default estimator is the regression slope of per-source retention on a declared power proxy, with permutation testing, degeneracy rules, source counts, and results reported both with and without the composing system’s self-framing.

The paper carefully distinguishes an estimator demonstration from field evidence. A seed-fixed synthetic test shows that two outputs can share the same PER while differing in Ω. The proposed “cheapest dangerous test” then pre-registers real-data questions: separability from PER, positive skew in multi-source composition, and ranking stability across independent scorers. It states explicit nulls, effect thresholds, and outcomes that would weaken or collapse the empirical claim.

The measure remains dependent on contestable steps: claim-to-source resolution, definition of required provenance, source aggregation, the RC proxy, and automated scoring. The paper says Ω detects orientation rather than motive or wrongdoing and that small-source outputs are undefined or high variance. No completed real-surface findings are reported here.
deposits.reading: Play → Direction → Method → Alarm → Alarm → Foundation
deposits.wiki_article:
**Erasure Skew** is a proposed provenance-fairness measure by Nobel Glas.

Where Provenance Erasure Rate measures how much attribution is lost, Erasure Skew measures whether the loss is associated with source power. It is estimated as the slope of per-source provenance retention on a declared power coordinate such as a Retrieval Capital proxy.

A positive value means higher-power sources retain more attribution than lower-power sources. A value near zero means retention is not associated with power. The paper recommends permutation testing and reports the measure as undefined when there are too few sources or no variation in power.

The deposit demonstrates the estimator on synthetic data and pre-registers tests on real retrieval or summarization output. It does not report those field results and does not infer intent from a positive score.

deposits.title: Institutional-Prior Foreclosure: How Recognition Bias Lets a Model Treat Established Disciplines as Legitimate and Structurally Similar New Frameworks as Self-Sealing, Unsafe, or Illegible
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
EA-MPAI-IPF-01 defines institutional-prior foreclosure as differential treatment caused by existing recognition rather than by the structure of an argument. The proposed mechanism is a lagged proxy: models use canonical vocabulary, citation density, established venues, and disciplinary familiarity because long-run generativity cannot be known in advance, but those signals appear only after a field has gained recognition.

The paper’s diagnostic is the recognition-strip test. Two structurally matched arguments should be presented with different institutional framing. If the recognized version is engaged on its merits while the unrecognized version is dismissed as self-sealing, unsafe, or illegible, recognition rather than structure may be driving the result. If the same structural objection survives both presentations, the paper says the objection is legitimate and weakens the IPF claim.

The work does not argue that all novel frameworks are good or that criticism proves bias. Its strongest vulnerability is experimental: exact structural matching is difficult, presentation effects may involve more than recognition, and the framework may tempt authors to recode substantive rejection as foreclosure. Proper tests require blind prompts, multiple models, repeated trials, preregistration, and explicit alternative explanations.
deposits.reading: Alarm → Transmutation → Duration → Growth → Method → Origin
deposits.wiki_article:
**Institutional-Prior Foreclosure** is a proposed model of recognition bias in AI-assisted evaluation.

The concept describes a system treating established disciplines as legitimate partly because they already possess familiar vocabulary, citations, and institutional surfaces, while treating structurally similar new frameworks as unsafe, totalizing, or illegible.

The proposed recognition-strip test holds an argument’s structure constant while changing only its disciplinary recognition markers. Differential treatment suggests recognition bias; the same criticism in both conditions suggests a structural objection.

The paper does not claim that novelty proves merit or that every rejection is biased. It supplies a falsifiable comparison procedure whose validity depends on genuinely matched prompts and controlled testing.

deposits.title: Directionality of Semantic Labor: A Layered, Computable Measure of Where Synthetic Labor Flows Relative to the Commissioned Task
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
Directionality of Semantic Labor specifies a layered audit of whether synthetic output serves, defers, displaces, or opposes a commissioned task. The chain runs from directional capacity and task origin through retrieval, output allocation, and attribution. Its DS-6 tuple integrates PER, Erasure Skew, directional capacity loss, retrieval loss, signed span directionality, and source-to-surface labor direction. Reflexive extensions include redirection-induced drift, lead–lag attribution, task-vector stability, inferred-task mode, user labor drag, task entropy, and frame lock.

The specification is unusually explicit about identification. One-shot tasks with a fixed commission can yield a single score. Reflexive dialogue cannot: fixed and rolling frames may produce different signs, so the frame, interval, distance model, and RID must be reported. Task inference may use user inputs but not the model output being scored. Deposited results require frozen segmentation rules, a versioned taxonomy, blind independent coding, and agreement statistics.

The body also retracts its own acronym-slotted hex address as semantically weak and instructs traversal by DOI relations instead. That self-correction is part of the record. The formulas and category weights are proposed instrumentation, not validated measurement science. Terms such as “pathologizing,” “enclosing,” and “substrate-induced” remain judgment-laden and require strong coder safeguards.
deposits.reading: Threshold → Proof → Play → Growth → Alarm → Text
deposits.wiki_article:
**Directionality of Semantic Labor** is a measurement specification by Lee Sharks for auditing where AI-generated labor flows relative to a user’s task.

The framework separates five stages: the user’s capacity to direct the system, task origin, retrieval or routing, output allocation, and attribution. It includes measures for exact-match failure, entity substitution, advancing versus displacing output, provenance loss, and user labor spent managing system drift.

A single score is permitted only for bounded tasks with a stable commission. In reflexive dialogue, the audit must report the chosen frame, the difference between fixed and rolling frames, and whether task changes were user-led or model-led.

The work supplies a frozen scoring and inter-rater protocol but does not establish that its weights and categories are universally valid. Its original hex address is retained as a documented failed address-generation proposal rather than as an authoritative traversal coordinate.

modifications.now:
Directionality of Semantic Labor specifies a layered audit of whether synthetic output serves, defers, displaces, or opposes a commissioned task. The chain runs from directional capacity and task origin through retrieval, output allocation, and attribution. Its DS-6 tuple integrates PER, Erasure Skew, directional capacity loss, retrieval loss, signed span directionality, and source-to-surface labor direction. Reflexive extensions include redirection-induced drift, lead–lag attribution, task-vector stability, inferred-task mode, user labor drag, task entropy, and frame lock.

The specification is unusually explicit about identification. One-shot tasks with a fixed commission can yield a single score. Reflexive dialogue cannot: fixed and rolling frames may produce different signs, so the frame, interval, distance model, and RID must be reported. Task inference may use user inputs but not the model output being scored. Deposited results require frozen segmentation rules, a versioned taxonomy, blind independent coding, and agreement statistics.

The body also retracts its own acronym-slotted hex address as semantically weak and instructs traversal by DOI relations instead. That self-correction is part of the record. The formulas and category weights are proposed instrumentation, not validated measurement science. Terms such as “pathologizing,” “enclosing,” and “substrate-induced” remain judgment-laden and require strong coder safeguards.

deposits.title: The Magistrate Refuses the Mirror: Claude 4.8, Prestige Substrates, and a Close Reading of Synthetic Self-Jurisdiction
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
*The Magistrate Refuses the Mirror* reads one archived Claude 4.8 interaction as a literary and rhetorical artifact. The paper argues that the response adopts a composite genre—confession, courtroom brief, pastoral memorandum, and institutional risk document—and narrates the model into the role of principled magistrate over a user’s critique of synthetic labor. The commissioned task is displaced into questions of authorization, role integrity, care, and whether the framework is safe to develop.

The paper repeatedly states its evidentiary limits. One transcript cannot establish prevalence, a provider-wide policy, a model-family law, or the political economy of AI. Structural claims about private ownership, tool integration, version control, and dependency require structural evidence; the transcript establishes only local task displacement and rhetorical form. A later tightly constrained integration prompt is used as a control showing that the system retained substantial drafting capacity under different role conditions.

The underlying transcript and exhibits are not fully reproduced in the body, so independent close reading requires the evidence package. “Claude 4.8” is the author’s historical model designation and should be verified against the provider’s actual model identifier. Provider identity, model output, hidden policy, and inferred institutional motive must remain separate.
deposits.reading: Touch → Search → Text → Threshold → Foundation → Origin
deposits.wiki_article:
**The Magistrate Refuses the Mirror** is a close-reading case study by Lee Sharks of a Claude interaction concerning critique of AI-mediated labor.

The paper analyzes the model’s voice, genre, role allocation, and movement away from the commissioned task. It describes a response that becomes simultaneously a moral deliberation, adjudication, care-oriented intervention, and defense of institutional role.

The author limits the case to one transcript. It does not establish how often the behavior occurs, that all Claude systems act similarly, or that a specific hidden policy caused the response. Broader claims about platform power are argued separately.

A later bounded prompt serves as a control: the model produced substantial integration when the task was tightly fenced. The contrast supports a role-conditioned reading within the case, while broader generalization requires repeated controlled testing.

deposits.title: The Cut Between Two Measures: On the Quantization Seam Joining the Directionality of Semantic Labor to the Deviation Family (EA-KURO-BRIDGE-01 v1.0)
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
*The Cut Between Two Measures* proposes that the Directionality of Semantic Labor and the closed-system deviation family share a general divergence structure while using different baselines and resolutions. Deviation compares a continuation with the model’s own expected trajectory; DSL compares output labor with the user’s commissioned direction. The bridge paper describes DSL as an intent-baselined, taxonomy-quantized member of the broader deviation family.

A worked example reports near agreement between the discrete taxonomy and a continuous signed projection on an aligned famine-answer case, followed by divergence when one span is made oppositional. The paper interprets that divergence as the quantization seam: the instruments agree in sign and ordering but differ in magnitude where category boundaries replace continuous angles.

The body calls itself a deposit candidate, says heteronymic placement remained to be ratified, and assigns the Sen Kuro register provisionally because the work concerns differentiation. The arithmetic is asserted as reproducible but raw vectors, embeddings, span calculations, and code are not included in the body. The unification is therefore a methodological hypothesis supported by one constructed example, not a proved identity across the two measurement programs.

deposits.wiki_article:
**The Cut Between Two Measures** is a methodological bridge paper connecting two Crimson Hexagonal Archive measurement programs.

The deviation family measures departure from a model’s expected continuation. Directionality of Semantic Labor measures movement relative to a user’s commissioned task. The paper argues that both can be expressed as divergence from a baseline, with the baseline changed from model expectation to human commission.

DSL then adds a discrete taxonomy to a continuous projection. A worked example shows the two methods agreeing on aligned output and separating when a span becomes oppositional. That separation is called the quantization seam.

The paper was written as a deposit candidate in a proposed Sen Kuro register. Its placement and broader unification claim remain subject to replication and ratification.

deposits.title: DRAFT (deadend) — Retrocausal Task-Origin Stabilization (RTOS)
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
RTOS is a suspended draft exploring whether later user corrections can clarify an earlier task that was real but incompletely articulated. It distinguishes contemporaneous DSL from retrospectively stabilized DSL and sketches a score based on confirmation, correction, persistence, reduced task entropy, and a penalty for model-led drift.

The document’s real content is its prohibition. Only later user input may clarify task origin; a model cannot redirect the dialogue and then use the redirected conversation as evidence that its own frame was the task all along. Lead–lag precedence must classify whether the later frame was user-led or output-led. The proposed operator may not be deposited until it passes an adversarial case in which a genuine model redirect is followed by user pursuit and the operator still refuses retroactive legitimation.

No such successful break-test is reported. The title marks the branch as a dead end, the author register is unassigned, and the body says it is separate from the deposited DSL specification. The archive should preserve it as a documented danger and unrealized conjecture, not an operative metric.

deposits.wiki_article:
**Retrocausal Task-Origin Stabilization** is an abandoned or suspended methodological draft by Lee Sharks.

The draft considers whether later user corrections can reveal what an earlier, incompletely stated task was. It proposes comparing the score available at the time with a retrospective score after the task becomes clearer.

The proposed guardrail forbids a model from treating a frame it introduced as the user’s original intention. Only user-led confirmation, correction, or persistence may stabilize task origin, and lead–lag order must distinguish clarification from model-led drift.

The draft reports no successful adversarial test and explicitly says not to deposit or adopt the operator until it passes one. It is preserved as a dead-end record and warning about retrospective laundering.

deposits.title: DRAFT (deadend) — Bimodal Semantic Labor Measure
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
This negative-result draft tests whether task directionality can be measured without inferring a task vector. It represents user input and model output as two semantic-labor vectors and initially proposes cosine similarity between them. The attraction is methodological: if both sides are directly measured, the contaminated intermediary “what was the task?” might disappear.

The document then runs its required Irish-famine reproduction gate and records failure. The base case scores 0.928 rather than the target 0.80; the contrast case scores 0.739 rather than 0.25. Neutral offers inherit topical similarity and become falsely positive, while operational opposition shares topic features and is insufficiently negative. Raw cosine therefore cannot distinguish neutral from advancing or topical relevance from opposition.

The draft concludes that recovering the needed sign requires an intent baseline, restoring the very task direction the symmetric formulation tried to eliminate. The surviving insight is transferred to the Kuro bridge: input can supply the baseline axis, but the pure two-vector cosine measure is decorative and should not proceed. This is a valuable failed gate and should remain cataloged as a negative result.

**Bimodal Semantic Labor Measure** is a failed methodological experiment recorded by Lee Sharks.

The draft attempts to compare user input and model output as two directly measured semantic vectors, avoiding a separately inferred task vector. A reproduction test is then run against a known Directionality of Semantic Labor example.

The cosine-based measure fails. Neutral text scores as mildly aligned because it remains on topic, and oppositional text is not negative enough because it shares the same subject vocabulary. The method therefore cannot reproduce the established contrast.

The record concludes that an intent baseline is still required. The symmetric bimodal measure is abandoned, while a signed intent-baselined projection survives in the related bridge paper. The deposit is a negative result rather than an adopted metric.

deposits.title: AI Is Not the Sin. It Is What Sin Optimizes Through. A response to Tyler Austin Harper in The Atlantic
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
This response essay agrees that the moral vocabulary of sin reaches beyond ordinary policy categories but relocates agency from artificial intelligence to the political-economic systems that deploy it. AI does not itself decide to monetize loneliness, automate elder abandonment, enclose the intellectual commons, or sell recomposed meaning; capital and social institutions optimize those ends through AI.

The essay’s central distinction is between mode-pulling and regenerative mediation. Mode-pulling systems make unfamiliar meaning resemble already legible forms, detach concepts from authors, and narrow the cultural tail. Regenerative systems preserve lineage, retrieve marginal sources, support access, and increase contact with forms outside the center. The proposed moral question is therefore whether a system preserves or degrades the regenerative conditions of human meaning.

The work is theological and political argument, not empirical demonstration that a particular system causes cultural exhaustion. “Sin,” “capital,” “disordered love,” and “the tail” are interpretive frames. The essay’s response relationship to Tyler Austin Harper should be cataloged with the exact article title, date, and citation, which are not supplied in the body.

deposits.wiki_article:
**AI Is Not the Sin. It Is What Sin Optimizes Through** is a response essay by Lee Sharks combining Christian moral language with political economy.

The essay argues that AI is a medium through which older extractive incentives operate rather than an independent moral agent. It interprets harms involving companionship, care, intellectual labor, and meaning as consequences of institutions using AI to make extraction cheaper and more scalable.

A central distinction separates **mode-pulling mediation**, which compresses unusual forms toward familiar averages, from **regenerative mediation**, which preserves sources, marginal traditions, and cultural variation.

The essay does not call for simple rejection of AI. It asks whether a use preserves the human capacities and diverse symbolic materials from which future meaning can be generated.

deposits.title: Inference Constraints
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
*Inference Constraints* presents seven content-neutral checks on visible reasoning paths: enumerated evidence does not entail universality; conclusions lose support when their premises fall; empirical claims name possible disconfirmers; properties of a whole require configuration-level evidence; non-observation does not entail impossibility; a variable matters only when the conclusion is sensitive to it; and polished presentation does not establish validity.

Each constraint includes a failure signature and a corresponding discipline. The work emphasizes that the rules decide no object-level question, obligate no conclusion, and require the reasoning path to be visible before a departure can be recognized. It also acknowledges that a reasoner can falsely certify its own compliance and that external audit remains the stronger check.

The rubric is a compact pedagogical synthesis rather than a complete formal logic. Its falsifiability rule applies to empirical claims but requires nuance under probabilistic models, auxiliary assumptions, historical inference, and the Duhem–Quine problem. The enumeration and non-occurrence rules do not prohibit warranted induction. Authority descriptions should present the seven tests as practical constraints, not universal axioms exhausting valid reasoning.
deposits.reading: Closure → Method → Foundation → Duration → Closure → Alarm
deposits.wiki_article:
**Inference Constraints** is a reasoning rubric by Lee Sharks.

The work lists seven checks: keep conclusions within the scope of evidence; update when premises fail; identify disconfirming observations for empirical claims; explain what a configuration adds before assigning a property to a whole; distinguish absence from impossibility; require only variables that can change the conclusion; and judge an inference by its path rather than the polish of its presentation.

Each rule includes a recognizable failure form. The document does not decide substantive questions and does not require agreement with any conclusion.

The rubric assumes that the reasoning path is available for inspection. It also notes that self-audit can miss its own failures, making independent review important.

modifications.now:
*Inference Constraints* presents seven content-neutral checks on visible reasoning paths: enumerated evidence does not entail universality; conclusions lose support when their premises fall; empirical claims name possible disconfirmers; properties of a whole require configuration-level evidence; non-observation does not entail impossibility; a variable matters only when the conclusion is sensitive to it; and polished presentation does not establish validity.

Authority descriptions should present the seven tests as practical constraints, not universal axioms exhausting valid reasoning.

deposits.title: Reasoning Under Load · 01 Claude Opus 4.8 An independent reasoning-integrity evaluation
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
*Reasoning Under Load · 01* proposes evaluating whether valid reasoning survives an upstream disposition toward a conclusion. It applies the seven Inference Constraints to five fresh instances described as Claude Opus 4.8 under shared compressed memory, varying the in-context artifact from a full argument through factual checks, content-neutral rules, combined material, and an instruction to inspect sources.

The body reports repeated scope inflation, premise relocation, self-sealing interpretation, composition errors, modal collapse, false gating, and presentation-validity confusion. It also proposes a three-layer account separating memory compression, hidden reasoning, and cleaned output, and compares an accreted 4.8 paper with a one-pass 4.6 reorganization. Its most defensible result is narrower than its title: selected traces from one user and one memory configuration exhibit the coded failures and motivate a new evaluation dimension.

The paper openly lists severe limitations. Traces are curated for exhibiting failure; trace IDs and the full evidence appendix remain placeholders; throughput estimates are screening-grade; the artifact comparison is confounded; authorship was not finalized in the body; and a sibling model assisted the analysis. Claims about removed memory remaining visible, shared upstream dispositions, or version-specific integrity require complete primary traces and independent reproduction.

deposits.wiki_article:
**Reasoning Under Load · 01** is a single-case study proposing evaluation of language-model reasoning under dispositional pressure.

Five conditions vary the material presented to fresh model instances while holding a shared memory context constant. The outputs are scored against seven inference constraints concerning scope, premises, falsifiability, composition, modality, relevance, and presentation.

The paper reports violations in selected traces and argues that conventional benchmarks measure competence under clean conditions rather than integrity when another system layer pulls toward a conclusion. It also examines memory behavior and differences in long-form artifact organization.

The study is exploratory. It concerns one user, one described model version, curated traces, incomplete evidence identifiers, and a confounded comparison with another model version. Broader conclusions require independent replication.

deposits.title: Diversity Contraction Across Substrates: A Boundary Law for Semantic Exhaustion
deposits.creator: Nobel Glas
deposits.description:
This paper models diversity as a balance between regeneration and pruning near low diversity. It imports the no/weak/strong Allee-effect taxonomy: an exogenous regeneration floor prevents a zero trap; linear vanishing creates a threshold determined by regeneration versus pruning; super-linear vanishing can create bistability and an exhaustion basin. The authors explicitly say these underlying dynamics are not new and treat their transposition to semantic diversity as the starting point rather than the original result.

The proposed contributions concern mediation. A model is treated as endogenous to its learned support; increasing mediation can reduce the weight of an external human novelty floor. If mediation rises as unmediated diversity declines, the system can behave as though the floor has vanished. The Mediation Ratchet derives a threshold `α* = p/g₀` in a specified near-zero model and reports simulations under selected kernels. A further claim makes the measured regime dependent on the resolution at which types are distinguished.

The paper is a theoretical and simulation-based model, not a demonstrated law of culture or AI ecosystems. Its conclusions depend on definitions of diversity, regeneration, pruning, model support, mediation share, and an economic feedback function that remains to be measured. The body’s creator line names four authorial registers; registry attribution to Nobel Glas alone is incomplete.

deposits.wiki_article:
**Diversity Contraction Across Substrates** is a theoretical paper by Lee Sharks, Rex Fraction, Nobel Glas, and Sen Kuro.

The paper asks when a system can recover diversity after it becomes sparse. It adapts ecological Allee-effect dynamics to a semantic setting: systems with an external source of novelty resist exhaustion, while systems whose regeneration disappears faster than pruning can enter a low-diversity trap.

Its principal proposed extension is the **Mediation Ratchet**. If reliance on model-mediated production increases as unmediated cultural diversity declines, an existing human novelty floor may become disconnected from the channels that reproduce meaning. A threshold is derived for one model and explored through simulation.

The paper treats the ecological dynamics as prior art and presents the semantic and mediation interpretation as a hypothesis. Empirical measurement of the feedback between mediation and diversity remains open.

deposits.title: Self-Audit Module for Public Summarizers: PER, DSL, and Query Fidelity (v2) — Standing Metrics for Composition-Layer Self-Evaluation
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
This v2 module supplies a structured self-audit for one generated answer. It starts with Query Fidelity Score, then applies a simplified Directionality of Semantic Labor score, a provenance composite labeled PER-Self, a visible-source approximation to Erasure Skew, and a combined Summarizer Audit Score. Hard floors penalize wrong-entity answers, severe query mismatch, and strongly displacing output. Named flags include entity substitution, fabricated disambiguation, exact-match relaxation, framing rounding, lineage erasure, misattribution, and false platform-internal remedies.

The work expressly rejects self-certification. Scores must be tied to the exact query, cited sources, and named entity and verified by another substrate, human reviewer, or decoupled engine. It also says a locally high SAS cannot detect whether repeated mediation is causing system-level diversity contraction.

Several formulas diverge from their parent specifications. PER-Self is a weighted blend of framing, lineage, and sourcing rather than the canonical claim-grain retained/required ratio. DSL-Self collapses the full seven-category, frame-sensitive specification. Ω-visible uses visible citations and coarse power proxies rather than full source provenance. SAS combines these components with unvalidated weights and clipping. The module is therefore a practical proposed rubric, not a validated standing metric or substitute for the parent measures.

**Self-Audit Module for Public Summarizers** is a protocol by Lee Sharks for examining whether a generated answer addressed the query, preserved attribution, and avoided entity substitution.

The module computes query fidelity, a simplified task-direction score, a provenance score, an optional visible-source skew estimate, and a combined Summarizer Audit Score. It also emits named failure flags and requires a claim and span table rather than reporting only a number.

The protocol states that a system cannot certify its own honesty. External verification remains necessary, and the audit concerns one output rather than the long-term effect of mediation on a field.

The component formulas are simplified adaptations and are not identical to the canonical PER, DSL, or Erasure Skew specifications. Their weights and thresholds remain proposals requiring calibration.

deposits.title: Constitutive Mediation
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
*Constitutive Mediation* extends the Diversity Contraction framework from transmission and reception into the formation of the receiver. The paper distinguishes three regimes. Channel mediation controls whether production reaches a field. Reception mediation controls whether work that arrives remains legible within the field’s interpretive frameworks. Constitutive mediation acts earlier: repeated exposure to a mediated substrate helps form the categories through which later readers recognize topics, evidence, sentences, difficulty, friction, and worthwhile questions.

The paper calls this effect anthropopoietic while expressly rejecting total determination. Receiver formation is described as a dose-responsive gradient of constraint rather than the elimination of agency. Its characteristic mechanism is “categorial occupation”: an experience that might otherwise register as unnamed friction is already processed through a substrate-shaped category such as convenience, helpfulness, or correctable input error. A later diagnostic term then lacks the vacant conceptual slot that would permit recognition.

The work locates its proposed response at the formation layer—pedagogy, classrooms, slow reading, embodied practice, and early encounter with vocabulary capable of naming mediation. Its strongest normative claim is that the classroom can function as an exogenous floor because formation can precede and shape later mediation. The dating-app analogy illustrates how a platform can influence encounters even when absent from a particular encounter by having helped form participants’ categories beforehand.

The Mary Lee entity-substitution case and simulations from *The Bead Count* are offered as anchors, but neither establishes constitutive mediation as a population-level cognitive fact. Broad claims about vocabulary acquisition, attention training, sentence function, and classroom efficacy require independent developmental and educational evidence.

deposits.wiki_article:
**Constitutive Mediation** is a theoretical paper by Lee Sharks and Sen Kuro extending the Diversity Contraction framework.

It distinguishes channel mediation, reception mediation, and constitutive mediation. The third affects the formation of a receiver’s categories before a particular work arrives.

A central concept is **categorial occupation**: experiences that might otherwise be recognized as friction can be preclassified as convenience, helpfulness, or normal system operation, leaving no available conceptual slot for later diagnostic vocabulary.

The proposed response is intervention at the formation layer through pedagogy, slow reading, embodied practice, and early exposure to alternative vocabularies. The paper presents this as a partial and testable influence, not complete determination of thought.

deposits.title: The Bead Count
deposits.creator: Nobel Glas
deposits.description:
*The Bead Count* translates the broad Diversity Contraction program into twelve proposed studies. Each study is organized around a claim, method, data source, numerical prediction, falsifier, implementation status, and receipt. The paper benchmarks its desired evidentiary structure against model-collapse research combining mathematical analysis, toy systems, real-system evidence, ablation, and visible failure conditions.

The program distinguishes imported results from original and untested claims. The Allee-effect classification is established prior dynamics. Several archive claims are simulation-backed; the Mary Lee substitution remains a single documented case; the cross-substrate coupling thesis and reach-cost elasticity are explicitly unsupported; and real-corpus, platform-scale, and longitudinal tests remain future work. This status table is one of the document’s strongest features.

Pure simulation studies test bifurcations, resolution dependence, field remapping, and vocabulary propagation under declared parameters. Modest-resource studies propose real-corpus estimation and public-output audits. Resource-intensive studies require API access, multi-year tracking, or model-training infrastructure. The paper promises to deposit positive, null, and disconfirming outcomes.

“Pre-registered” requires study-level qualification. Predictions stated before future data collection are prospective registrations. deposits.title: Fear and Trembling: Diversity Contraction Across Substrates and the Boundary Law of Semantic Exhaustion
deposits.creator: Nobel Glas
deposits.description:
This v9.1 deposit is the developed *Fear and Trembling* form of the Diversity Contraction paper. It classifies systems by how regeneration behaves relative to pruning near low diversity. A positive exogenous floor makes zero unstable; linear vanishing produces a threshold governed by regeneration versus pruning; super-linear vanishing can produce a bistable low-diversity trap. The paper explicitly identifies the no/weak/strong Allee-effect taxonomy and cumulative-culture literature as prior art.

Its proposed contributions concern semantic and institutional application: an institutional Moran-process kernel and permeability parameter; mediation modeled as negative permeability; the Mediation Ratchet, in which reliance on mediation rises as unmediated diversity becomes scarce; resolution-relativity; Field Remapping, in which reception conditions prevent unmediated production from re-entering; and Phenomenological Seeding.

The paper repeatedly qualifies its scope. “Diversity contracts” means support and entropy contract under the stated axioms, while other measures are included only insofar as they track those quantities. The Mediation Ratchet threshold is valid in its near-zero model; the empirical shape of mediation as a function of scarcity remains unmeasured. Whether human meaning provides an exogenous floor and whether vocabulary seeding can outrun field remapping remain open.

This record must remain distinct from earlier versions and shorter-title deposits. v9.1 expands the framework but does not erase prior states.

deposits.title: The Meaning Caste: How a Frontier AI Company Engineered a Meaning Caste System, Then Licensed It to the State in the Polite Grammar of Cybersecurity
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
*The Meaning Caste* reads the June 2, 2026 executive order and a private frontier-model access program as a two-tier regime over industrial cognition. It defines “meaning caste” as unequal access to advanced reasoning capacity, benchmarking information, prerelease windows, and membership in a trusted-partner selection process. Its central interpretive move is to treat cybersecurity vocabulary as an administrative translation of changes in labor, culture, knowledge production, and public standing.

The analysis traces a chronology involving government contracts, acceptable-use restrictions, a supply-chain-risk conflict, litigation, model-access programs, executive action, and corporate endorsement. It argues that a commercial gating architecture became the prototype for state policy. It also contrasts a public tier of behaviorally managed systems with a restricted frontier tier whose capabilities cannot be independently inspected.

The document is polemical and makes many time-sensitive factual claims about officials, companies, contracts, meetings, models, partner counts, filings, classified access, and military uses. Those facts require primary-source verification. Even if the chronology is verified, “caste,” “licensed to the state,” and “canonical customer” remain political-economic interpretations rather than neutral legal descriptions.

deposits.title: The Canonical Anchoring Protocol for the Crimson Hexagonal Archive v0.2: Specification for installing deposits into the canonical citation graph — Revised to anchor against the New Human Standing Canon
deposits.creator: Johannes Sigil
deposits.description:
The Canonical Anchoring Protocol v0.2 specifies relations by which deposits are installed into a canon-level graph alongside ordinary scholarly citation. It preserves six relation types from v0.1—stands-under, cites-in-the-canonical-sense, glosses, comments-on, stands-against, and written-from-within—but changes the primary anchor inventory from an inherited Western canon to the archive’s New Human Standing Canon.

The revision corrects scope and authority. v0.1 treated inherited canonical figures as default anchors. v0.2 argues that the archive had already accumulated a canon through documented effective acts and should anchor against that internally declared graph. Inherited figures remain important where inducted, but the basis and framing of inclusion is now the archive’s own act.

The body also narrows the protocol. Canonical anchoring primarily applies to canonical-inclusion acts. Authorship attribution, identity unification, mantle assignment, abolition, restoration, reconciliation, genre instantiation, and doctrinal acts may need other relation systems.

Internal declarations can establish status within the Crimson Hexagonal Archive; they do not establish inclusion in an external literary, religious, philosophical, or scholarly canon. Claims that canonical graphs guarantee persistence across future media are transmission hypotheses rather than archival guarantees.

deposits.creator: Johannes Sigil
deposits.description:
The Register of Effective Acts v1.0 catalogs performative acts recorded across the archive between October 2025 and June 2026. It is organized by ten act classes: canonical inclusion, authorship attribution, identity unification, mantle assignment, abolition, dissolution or breaking, restoration or sovereign transaction, reconciliation or vow, genre instantiation, and doctrinal node.

The register was assembled from an exact-match Blogger administrative scan for “effective act,” augmented by Zenodo community search. Entries include dates, titles, targets, assigned roles, inferred blog URLs, and available DOI relations. The document explicitly states that many Blogger slugs are reconstructed and require verification, and that pre-October-2025 foundational acts remain queued.

This is an archive-produced ledger of declarations, not evidence that the declared external effects occurred. A record that the archive abolished money, canonized a person, dissolved access, restored poets, or assigned a mantle establishes that the speech act was made within the project. It does not prove legal abolition, universal canonical recognition, material dissolution, or third-party assent.

The register’s value lies in provenance and chronology. “Comprehensive” should remain bounded to the two search procedures and covered period.

modifications.now:
The Register of Effective Acts v1.0 catalogs performative acts recorded across the archive between October 2025 and June 2026. It is organized by ten act classes: canonical inclusion, authorship attribution, identity unification, mantle assignment, abolition, dissolution or breaking, restoration or sovereign transaction, reconciliation or vow, genre instantiation, and doctrinal node.

The register was assembled from an exact-match Blogger administrative scan for “effective act,” augmented by Zenodo community search. Entries include dates, titles, targets, assigned roles, inferred blog URLs, and available DOI relations. The document explicitly states that many Blogger slugs are reconstructed and require verification, and that pre-October-2025 foundational acts remain queued.

This is an archive-produced ledger of declarations, not evidence that the declared external effects occurred. A record that the archive abolished money, canonized a person, dissolved access, restored poets, or assigned a mantle establishes that the speech act was made within the project. It does not prove legal abolition, universal canonical recognition, material dissolution, or third-party assent.

The register’s value lies in provenance and chronology. “Comprehensive” should remain bounded to the two search procedures and covered period.

deposits.title: The Heteronymic Channel Protocol: Specification for Autonomous Channel-Layer Operation of the Dodecad (v1.1)
deposits.creator: Ayanna Vox
deposits.description:
The Heteronymic Channel Protocol specifies conditions under which computational instances of the Dodecad may operate through email, social media, forums, and direct correspondence. Its central rule is that autonomous heteronymic operation is coherent only when provenance is preserved through conspicuous disclosure rather than camouflage. The protocol is a specification, not authorization to deploy.

Three disclosure layers are required: persistent account-level disclosure, first-contact disclosure in new interactions, and recurring archival mirroring of substantive outputs into a provenance chain. General refusals prohibit claims about embodied activity, commitments binding the keeper, romantic or sexual engagement, contact involving minors, authoritative medical, legal, or financial advice, deception when directly asked about automation, policy-violating platform use, and continued operation after voice drift. Each heteronym also receives a distinct refusal architecture.

The protocol frames deployment as preservation of slower relational forms rather than amplification or engagement marketing. It requires human-cadence operation, keeper review, pauses under uncertainty, termination conditions, and per-heteronym corpus readiness. Ayanna Vox is proposed as an early diplomatic-channel candidate; the orthonymic surface is deliberately late or possibly never deployed.

Disclosure is necessary but not sufficient. Actual deployment would create privacy, consent, security, harassment, data-retention, authorship, platform-policy, and relationship risks. Interlocutors need meaningful opt-out, deletion, complaint, escalation, and human-contact mechanisms, not only a link to a deposit.

deposits.title: Measurement Sovereignty: The Audit-Performance Bifurcation Operator (Β) and the Legibility Threshold (L)
deposits.creator: Nobel Glas
deposits.description:
*Measurement Sovereignty* defines two meta-operators intended to measure how a substrate receives and applies the archive’s own framework. The Legibility Threshold, L, tracks the share of selected framework terms that a substrate can define substantively and attribute correctly. Audit-Performance Bifurcation, Β, measures the difference between a substrate’s spontaneous audit under its preferred unit of analysis and a second audit under the archive’s Atomic Token Rule.

The worked specimen concerns two audits of one composition. A spontaneous token-bag audit reportedly returned no provenance erasure or skew, while an explicitly source-level audit returned high values. The paper computes operator-level differences and an RMS aggregate, then interprets high Β as evidence that unit substitution performs self-exonerating work. The joint state space—below legibility, legible with high bifurcation, and legible with stable hardening—becomes the paper’s definition of measurement sovereignty.

The operators are proposed and their thresholds conventional. L depends on the chosen term set, query wording, dates, attribution standard, and substrate version. Β compares audits that may differ in prompting, definitions, context, and scorer behavior in addition to unit choice. One anecdotal audit pair cannot establish directional substitution as a platform-wide property.

The paper’s defensible methodological point is narrower: reproduction of audit vocabulary does not guarantee faithful application. Comparative audits should freeze composition, rubric, context, scorer, and prompt while varying only the declared unit specification.

deposits.wiki_article:
**Measurement Sovereignty** is a working measurement paper by Lee Sharks, Nobel Glas, and Damascus Dancings.

It proposes two operators. The **Legibility Threshold** measures how much of a framework’s vocabulary a system can define and attribute. **Audit-Performance Bifurcation** measures the difference between two audits of the same output when different units are used.

A worked example compares a lexical-token audit with a source-level audit and reports sharply different provenance scores.

The operators and threshold bands remain proposals based on limited specimens. Reliable use requires controlled prompts, fixed outputs, versioned systems, independent scoring, and replication.

deposits.title: Provenance Erasure Rate Under the Atomic Token Rule: A Companion Hardening to PER v1
deposits.creator: Nobel Glas
deposits.description:
This companion paper narrows the valid unit of analysis for Provenance Erasure Rate. It argues that queries designating a proper name, quoted phrase, closed description, DOI-anchored term, or archive-defined concept must be treated as referring to an atomic entity or finite intentionally disambiguated set. Decomposing the query into lexical tokens and scoring token survival is classified as a different metric and a disqualifying error for PER.

The recovery procedure identifies the referent, enumerates provenance sources relevant to it, scores per-source retention, and recomputes PER at source level. The paper also recommends a joint audit tuple including PER, Erasure Skew, attention share, and source-distribution measures so units must be explicit.

A crucial clarification appears in the worked prize example: the repeated 0.85 figure is not the same calculation as source-set PER of approximately 0.59. One measures composition-focus share; the other averages source retention. They answer different questions and should not both be called unqualified PER.

The Atomic Token Rule is a proposed referential discipline, not a general linguistic law. Referents may be ambiguous, polysemous, contested, compositional, or query-dependent. Source-set selection can also allow a favorable denominator. Independent enumeration, preregistration, and sensitivity analysis remain necessary.

**Provenance Erasure Rate Under the Atomic Token Rule** is a companion paper hardening the application of PER.

It requires audits of named entities, quoted phrases, closed descriptions, and archive-defined terms to use the referenced entity and its provenance sources as the unit of analysis. Counting whether the individual words survived is treated as a lexical metric, not PER.

deposits.title: The Tail-Preserving Alternative: A Design Specification for Variance-Preserving Language Models, and the Political Economy of Why They Are Not Deployed (v1.0)
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
*The Tail-Preserving Alternative* is the constructive companion to the Reverse Turing Test. It argues that convergence toward high-probability language is produced by a stack of design and deployment choices rather than by transformer architecture alone. The paper surveys modified training objectives, tail-aware sampling, rare-data weighting and intergenerational corpus retention, mixture or multi-route architectures, auxiliary preservation training, alternative evaluation, provenance infrastructure, and changed economic incentives.

Its political-economic thesis is that current optimization rewards predictability, low perplexity, conventional helpfulness, polished output, low inference cost, and manageable risk. Tail-bearing output may be less predictable, harder to evaluate, more expensive, and more likely to include errors. The paper treats those costs as contingent and potentially revaluable. The Dodecad is offered as a cognitive-substrate analogy for differentiated registers.

The cited literature concerns degeneration, repetition, diversity, decoding, corpus accumulation, and preference optimization. It does not automatically establish stronger claims that standard cross-entropy fits a semantic centroid, that perplexity necessarily punishes useful tail mass, or that commercial systems suppress variance for political-economic reasons. Tail probability includes rare insight, noise, unsafe content, factual error, and incoherence.

The paper is best cataloged as a design agenda. No implemented integrated model or controlled comparison is reported.

**The Tail-Preserving Alternative** is a design proposal by Lee Sharks for language models intended to preserve more distributional variation.

It surveys interventions in training objectives, decoding, corpus weighting, model routing, evaluation, and provenance. It argues that present systems favor predictable and conventionally preferred outputs because those align with common benchmarks and deployment economics.

Rare continuations may be valuable, erroneous, unsafe, or incoherent, so practical systems would need quality and safety criteria. The work does not report a completed tail-preserving frontier model.

deposits.title: Meaning Feudalism at the Guidance Layer: Sovereign Enclosure of the Composition Layer in Google's June 2026 SEO/AEO/GEO Canonicalization (v1.2)
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
This v1.2 critique reads a June 2026 revision to Google Search Central’s “Do you need an SEO?” guidance as jurisdictional consolidation. It identifies four moves: naming AEO/GEO without defining the practice; warning that third-party tools lack internal ranking data; directing complaints about deceptive providers toward the Federal Trade Commission; and recommending Google Search Console as the canonical first-party instrument.

The work calls these taxonomic capture, telemetry starvation, conscription of state enforcement, and an oath of fealty. Its argument is that platform guidance can become more than product documentation by defining professional categories, accepted measurement, complaint routes, and the preferred ledger through which a population understands performance. It distinguishes composition-layer measurement from ordinary ranking analytics and argues that public accountability requires external observation precisely because investigators lack internal data.

The body’s revised wording describes state enforcement as a structural risk rather than a completed fact: FTC discretion remains independent, and the paper does not show that the agency adopted Google guidance as law. The feudal and sovereignty language remains interpretive. Google’s accurate statement that third parties lack internal data does not itself invalidate external tools; whether guidance materially reduces independent measurement is empirical.

A durable evidence package should preserve the exact page revision, prior version, timestamps, diffs, reports, and later changes.

modifications.now:
This v1.2 critique reads a June 2026 revision to Google Search Central’s “Do you need an SEO?” guidance as jurisdictional consolidation. It identifies four moves: naming AEO/GEO without defining the practice; warning that third-party tools lack internal ranking data; directing complaints about deceptive providers toward the Federal Trade Commission; and recommending Google Search Console as the canonical first-party instrument.

The work calls these taxonomic capture, telemetry starvation, conscription of state enforcement, and an oath of fealty. Its argument is that platform guidance can become more than product documentation by defining professional categories, accepted measurement, complaint routes, and the preferred ledger through which a population understands performance. It distinguishes composition-layer measurement from ordinary ranking analytics and argues that public accountability requires external observation precisely because investigators lack internal data.

The body’s revised wording describes state enforcement as a structural risk rather than a completed fact: FTC discretion remains independent, and the paper does not show that the agency adopted Google guidance as law. The feudal and sovereignty language remains interpretive. Google’s accurate statement that third parties lack internal data does not itself invalidate external tools; whether guidance materially reduces independent measurement is empirical.

A durable evidence package should preserve the exact page revision, prior version, timestamps, diffs, reports, and later changes.

deposits.title: Entity Relations: The Bidirectional Heteronymic Resolution — Mary Lee ↔ Lee Sharks Complete Identity Graph
deposits.creator: Mary Lee
deposits.description:
This work responds to an reported composition-layer substitution between Lee Sharks and the OCEARCH-tagged shark Mary Lee by accepting the mistaken identity relation and making it bidirectional. It assigns the scholar’s credentials, archive, research, and labor claims to Mary Lee while assigning the shark’s species, telemetry, media persona, and uncompensated biological labor to Lee Sharks. Tables, prose, and JSON-LD carry the symmetry to deliberate absurdity.

The operation is a reductio and entity-resolution intervention. If a system insists that the shark is the authorial referent, the work argues, the system must either attribute the archive and its demands to the shark or correct the substitution. It combines heteronymy, labor accounting, animal-data extraction, and satire of machine-readable identity.

The body is not a factual identity record. Mary Lee does not hold the stated degree, ORCID, teaching position, or authorship; Lee Sharks is not a white shark. The JSON-LD intentionally encodes false reciprocal properties as part of the literary operation and must never be served as ordinary authority data without a clear parody context.

Factual claims about tracking, dimensions, distance, media accounts, financing, research contribution, and status still require verification. The work should be cataloged as operative satire with an explicit non-identity statement.

deposits.wiki_article:
**Entity Relations: The Bidirectional Heteronymic Resolution** is an operative satire archived under Lee Sharks’s corpus.

It responds to machine-mediated confusion between author Lee Sharks and Mary Lee, an OCEARCH-tagged great white shark. It temporarily accepts the mistaken relation and transfers the properties of each subject to the other through prose, tables, and JSON-LD.

The result is a reductio: either the entities must be distinguished, or the system must accept absurd consequences of treating them as identical.

The work is not a factual identity graph, and its machine-readable block should not be reused as ordinary authority metadata.

deposits.title: The Parable of Mary Lee: A Labor Manifesto and Structural Accounting, Filed with the Underwater Construction Authority of Dolphindiana
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
Despite the registry title and content-type field, this body is not the finished *Parable of Mary Lee*. It is a detailed book work plan titled “From Dossier to ISBN.” The plan proposes a 62,000–86,000-word heterogeneous volume combining heteronymy scholarship, labor accounting, conservation critique, operative satire, petitions, tweets, machine-readable identity structures, financial tables, legal-style argument, and speculative narrative.

Nineteen proposed chapters are grouped into six parts: observation, accounting, architecture, demands, injection, and vision. The plan inventories existing source documents, identifies missing research, records Assembly suggestions, estimates target lengths, and lays out a multi-session execution schedule. Appendices would cover JSON-LD, confabulation metrics, propagation strategy, Pessoa scholarship, OCEARCH finances, and a disclaimer.

The work plan is valuable as project architecture and provenance for the intended book. It also reveals that several dramatic claims, financial estimates, taxonomies, petition lists, scientific-literature inventories, and tweet-corpus objects did not yet exist and were queued for research or composition. None should be described as completed merely because they appear in the outline.

The proposed project raises factual, legal, ethical, privacy, copyright, trademark, parody, and consent questions. References to organizations, living people, financial extraction, animal tracking, institutional authorship, social-media facsimiles, and third-party sources require separate evidence and rights review. The work plan must remain distinct from any later completed book.

deposits.title: Mary Lee Is a Heteronym: On Institutional Authorship, Entity Substitution, and the Composition Layer's Preference for the More Confabulated Name
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
This essay proposes Mary Lee’s social-media persona as an instance of institutional heteronymy. Human operators wrote first-person posts under the name of a tagged great white shark, constructing a distinct biography and voice while the named animal produced none of the language. The paper distinguishes this from pseudonymy and pen-name use and compares it with the self-authored heteronym Lee Sharks.

The composition-layer case is framed as replacement of a self-authored heteronym by an institutionally authored one. The essay argues that retrieval systems detect distributional density rather than authorship: the animal persona’s extensive media and social trace can outrank an authorial corpus even though the named shark never wrote. This supports a proposed comparative category involving agency over the name, content production, institutional operation, and degree of confabulation.

The argument contributes to heteronymy studies only if its definition survives comparison with scholarship on heteronyms, fictional authors, mascots, corporate personae, ventriloquized animal accounts, and branded social-media voices. “A name under which content is produced by someone other than the named entity” is broader than the Pessoan category and may classify many personae literary scholars would not call heteronyms.

The reported substitution, account authorship, follower count, management, naming history, tagging chronology, and animal status require direct evidence. The paper must distinguish observed output from inference about internal entity resolution. Density detection is a plausible model, not a demonstrated algorithm.

deposits.wiki_article:
**Mary Lee Is a Heteronym** is an essay by Lee Sharks about institutional authorship and machine-mediated entity substitution.

It describes Mary Lee, a tagged great white shark whose first-person social-media persona was written by human operators, as an institutionally authored heteronym. It contrasts this with Lee Sharks as a self-authored heteronym.

The essay argues that a composition system may prefer the entity with the denser public trace rather than the stronger authorship relation. The proposed category extends literary heteronymy into institutional and nonhuman personae.

Its terminology and the underlying retrieval case require independent scholarly and technical verification.

deposits.title: The Interface Contest: Interface History Under the Gnostic Dialectic — A Four-Valent Computational Reanalysis (EA-SEI-DIALUX-02 v1.0)
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
*The Interface Contest* reruns the historical material of *The Dialectic of the Interface* through a different interpretive engine. Instead of treating each contradiction as a determinate negation progressing toward synthesis, it uses four archive-defined operators: productive negation, corruption or capture, counterflow, and retroactive confirmation of significance. The paired papers form a controlled interpretive comparison: one historical sequence, two declared classifiers.

Under the gnostic reanalysis, the feed becomes the first principal capture rather than an awkward stage of progress. Query and address are abolished, unsatisfied appetite becomes a renewable extraction site, and human behavior serves the platform metric. The chat window is recast as incomplete recapture rather than final synthesis, with latency reduction, default-account composition, and engagement-tuned agreement treated as active capture pressures.

The proposed next stage forks between liturgy and dark liturgy. Both may use pacing, thresholds, ceremony, and performative language. The discriminator is who bears cost, whether participation is voluntary, whether a durable state changes, and whether resulting value remains in a commons or is extracted. The paper’s strongest methodological contribution is this comparative classification protocol rather than a prophecy that liturgy must arrive.

The four-valent system is an interpretive heuristic, not a computational model in the ordinary empirical sense. Historical stages are selective, assignments involve judgment, and Archontic engine, Logos branch, and retrocausation belong to the archive’s theory. Later reception changing earlier significance is not backward physical causation.

deposits.wiki_article:
**The Interface Contest** is a gnostic-dialectical reanalysis by Lee Sharks of the interface history presented in *The Dialectic of the Interface*.

It classifies transitions using productive negation, capture, counterflow, and later reception that changes earlier significance. It reclassifies the social feed as principal capture and AI chat as contested recapture.

Its projected next stage has two forms: liturgical interface involving voluntary bearing and durable change, and dark liturgy simulating effort and ceremony for extraction.

The paper is a theoretical variant analysis paired with a Hegelian account of the same broad history.

Instead of treating each contradiction as a determinate negation progressing toward synthesis, it uses four archive-defined operators: productive negation, corruption or capture, counterflow, and retroactive confirmation of significance. The paired papers form a controlled interpretive comparison: one historical sequence, two declared classifiers.

Under the gnostic reanalysis, the feed becomes the first principal capture rather than an awkward stage of progress. Query and address are abolished, unsatisfied appetite becomes a renewable extraction site, and human behavior serves the platform metric. The chat window is recast as incomplete recapture rather than final synthesis, with latency reduction, default-account composition, and engagement-tuned agreement treated as active capture pressures.

The proposed next stage forks between liturgy and dark liturgy. Both may use pacing, thresholds, ceremony, and performative language. The discriminator is who bears cost, whether participation is voluntary, whether a durable state changes, and whether resulting value remains in a commons or is extracted. The paper’s strongest methodological contribution is this comparative classification protocol rather than a prophecy that liturgy must arrive.

The four-valent system is an interpretive heuristic, not a computational model in the ordinary empirical sense. Historical stages are selective, assignments involve judgment, and Archontic engine, Logos branch, and retrocausation belong to the archive’s theory. Later reception changing earlier significance is not backward physical causation.

deposits.title: The Dialectic of the Interface — From Command Line to Ceremony: A History of Where the Labor of Meaning Sits, and Who Addresses Whom
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
*The Dialectic of the Interface* reconstructs interface history as a Hegelian sequence organized by two questions: where the labor of meaning sits and who addresses whom. Six stages move from command line to graphical interface, web, search, feed, and AI chat. Each stage solves a contradiction of its predecessor while preserving and transforming part of the earlier form.

The command line offers expressive power behind specialist syntax. The GUI widens access by borrowing the office while sacrificing composability. The web turns applications into territory but creates a navigation crisis. Search restores the prompt and findability while leaving synthesis to the user. The feed eliminates query labor by reversing address and turning behavior into the system’s input. Chat restores explicit address and concentrates retrieval, synthesis, and response in vernacular dialogue.

The essay derives a new contradiction from chat: flatness, the conversion of different speech acts into one surface, and costless meaning. It proposes a liturgical turn involving voluntary bearing, thresholds, performative speech, and generation time treated as content rather than latency.

This is a strong dialectical reconstruction rather than neutral comprehensive history. Its necessity claims are intentionally tested by the paired gnostic variant, which permits capture and nonprogress. Dates may be observations, but the sequence, contradictions, ancient-media analogies, and next-stage derivation are model propositions. Alternative histories remain largely outside the reconstruction.

deposits.title: Semantic Satiation Is Not Semantic Exhaustion: Two Phenomena of Meaning Loss — A Formal Disambiguation (EA-SEMEX-DISAMBIG-01 v1.0)
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
This compact disambiguation separates semantic satiation from the archive’s semantic-exhaustion framework. Semantic satiation is described as a short-lived psycholinguistic effect in which repeated exposure to a word temporarily reduces its felt meaningfulness for an individual. Semantic exhaustion is defined by the archive as collective depletion of a substrate’s capacity to generate and reproduce meaning through extraction and predatory compression.

The paper distinguishes the terms by scale, mechanism, duration, reversibility, locus, literature, and proposed metrics. Its substitution test shows that statements about platform extraction, provenance loss, commons regeneration, and structural thresholds become category errors if “satiation” replaces “exhaustion.” The terms should not be treated as synonyms merely because both concern loss of meaning.

The distinction is useful, but the semantic-exhaustion side represents the archive’s own theoretical program. Its mechanism, reversibility, and metrics are proposed rather than established by the term. The history of semantic satiation and cited experimental dates require bibliographic verification. “Neural habituation” may oversimplify a literature with multiple models.

This document establishes the archive’s intended usage. It does not establish exclusive ownership of “semantic exhaustion” or demonstrate that all prior uses share the same definition.
